title: Beauty Talks with Miss United Continents US 2018 Jessica Jewel VanGaalen
dek: The 27-year-old Jessica VanGaalen was awarded the title of Miss United Continents US 2018 just a few weeks ago. The international pageant is all set to hold its grand finale on 7th September 2018 in Ecuador. Countries from various parts of the world send…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss United Continents US 2018 Jessica Jewel VanGaalen
paragraphs: The 27-year-old Jessica VanGaalen was awarded the title of Miss United Continents US 2018 just a few weeks ago. The international pageant is all set to hold its grand finale on 7th September 2018 in Ecuador. Countries from various parts of the world send their representatives to participate at this prestigious competition.
As she prepares to represent United States at Miss United Continents 2018, she finds time to talk about her guilty pleasures, ambitions and dreams with us in an exclusive interview.
Q. How does it feel to be Miss United Continents US 2018 and now a delegate of Miss United Continents 2018?
It feels amazing. I’m so blessed to represent the USA again on the International stage and am honored I’ve been selected to compete for such a prestigious title.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss United Continents US 2018?
I’ve learned to truly be yourself and to not be who you “think” the judges will want. When you are honest and real, you have more of an impact around you.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?
God. I am really fortunate to have my faith because it is God who has inspired me and helped me get through all the tough times and obstacles in my life.
Q. You also represented United States at Miss Eco International 2018. How was that experience for you?

It was such an amazing and unforgettable experience! I had dreamed about going to Egypt for a long time, so seeing that dream come to life AND getting to represent my home country was a once in a lifetime experience. I’m grateful for the memories and friendships that I have as a result of Miss Eco International.
Q. Who is your ideal, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

There are so many people who have came before me that led the way for today’s generation. It’s hard to pick one person, but I can say that every leader and role model of mine has stood up for themselves, the people around them and the generations to come. Fighting for women’s rights, the abolition of slavery, equality, and unification of nations… Inspiring! I hope to encourage and inspire more people to get involved in their communities and to teach the next generation to learn from our mistakes.
Q . How would you like to represent yourself at the international stage of Miss United Continents 2018?

I want to represent myself with class, charisma, humility and compassion. I want to leave knowing that I represented the USA in the most positive and loving manner. I think people get caught up in what social media or a government official says… But we ALL have our own opinions and I want everyone to remember THAT side to America. That equality, peace, love, unification and respect is deserved all around the world and I want that to come across as I represent the USA at Miss United Continents 2018.
Q . If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
I would spend my day watching and listening to people all over the world. I would love to be able to tune in to different countries and see what society is like when no one is looking.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My favorite memory would be riding roller coasters with my family. My dad passed away when I was 18 and I never realized how much I would miss his silly personality. He used to make scary noises on the Pirates of Caribbean at Disneyland… I never realized it as a kid, but he made the rides extra memorable and thrilling.
Q. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

My mom and dad. My dad passed away before he had a chance to watch me grow into a strong, independent woman. I believe he’s watching over me from heaven and is proud of everything I’ve accomplished. As for my mom, she’s been through so much throughout her life, but she always stays positive and continues to sacrifice for her kids.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Coke Icees, hands down! I used to go to Circle K almost daily for my Coke Icee but now I go to Burger King because I moved to California and there are no Circle K ice machines nearby.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

Honestly, I want to walk off the stage as the new Miss United Continents 2018. In all reality though, as long as I try my hardest and I impact at least one person in Ecuador, then I will be proud of myself. Sometimes it’s not about a title, but how you use your voice to impact those around you. I want to experience Ecuador and leave knowing I impacted someone’s life.
Q. If you were granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
I would wish for money to help my family get out of debt, for everyone to have unconditional love (not just for people they know, but for everyone), and lastly for true happiness.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?
Thank you so much for believing in me! I love all of you and hope I make you proud. Remember to always be yourself and let your love shine through.

dek: At the grand finale of 2018 UK Power Pageant held in June 2018, Joey Staerkle was crowned Miss Intercontinental Wales 2018. As Joey prepares for her international pageant Miss Intercontinental 2018 where she’ll represent Wales, she finds time to talk about…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Intercontinental Wales 2018 Joey Staerkle
paragraphs: At the grand finale of 2018 UK Power Pageant held in June 2018, Joey Staerkle was crowned Miss Intercontinental Wales 2018. As Joey prepares for her international pageant Miss Intercontinental 2018 where she’ll represent Wales, she finds time to talk about her dreams, ambitions and more in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q . How does it feel to be crowned Miss Intercontinental Wales 2018 and now a delegate of Miss Intercontinental 2018?
It’s a great honour to have won the title amongst such amazing competition, I look forward to carrying on the traditions of Queens before me and hope to do the title justice and make people proud.
Q . What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of the United Kingdom Power Pageant 2018?
To believe in yourself always and that things are always possible if you work hard.
Q . What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?
All that people that told me I couldn’t do something or would never make anything of myself, never let that negative energy drag you down instead use it to drive you forward and be better always.
Q . How would you like to represent yourself at the international stage of Miss Intercontinental 2018?
I would like to represent myself as I am, hard working, ambitious, with a good heart and trying to help others.
Q . Who is your idol, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

My parents, they raised me to not waste time on frivolous things, and to work hard and believe in myself, and to be successful both in life and business just as they have done, I hope I can be as successful as they have proven themselves to be.
Q . If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I’d spend the day in one of the city centres, seeing how homeless people are treated, being invisible I think is the only way you would truly get to see something like that without being in that situation yourself, and maybe you could learn how to help them more, and appreciate things you have in life that we take for granted so much more.
Q . Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

One year my nana who is no longer with us, made Easter truly magical one year as she decorated her garden with Easter eggs, decorations and real bunnies, as a small girl it was the most amazing thing that I have never forgotten and I swear I saw fairies in the trees that day, and still believe in them to this day. You should never lose the magic from your life, my nana taught me that.
Q . What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard everyday?

I empower myself,I don’t think we should be passengerswhen it comes to shaping our own lives, soI always make sure I am in the driver’s seat. I am very driven for success and I believe working hard now will pay off later. I enjoy working on constantly expanding my knowledge base and experiences, I try to grasp as many opportunities as I can. You are never too old to learn new things!
Q . What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
I really enjoy demolishing Mc Donald’s cheeseburgers with sour cream.
Q . We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?
I want to feel a sense of achievement and satisfaction when I look back on my life, knowing I have truly pushed myself and chased every experience and opportunity presented to me.
Q . If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
To be able to heal the sick,
Bring back lost family members,
Stop animal cruelty including animal testing, there is no need for such cruelty and suffering.
Q . Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?
Thank you so so much for all your support and messages, the road to pageant finals can be long and stressful but so rewarding when you see people supporting you along the way!

title: Beauty Talks with Jewel of the World 2018 Neena Macaire Bezuidenhout
dek: Jewel of the World 2018 held its grand finale on 26th May 2018 at the Dance Vision Arena, San Juan City, Philippines where Neena Macaire Bezuidenhout was crowned the first ever winner! The 21-year-old South African queen gave a spectacular performance at the…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Jewel of the World 2018 Neena Macaire Bezuidenhout
paragraphs: Jewel of the World 2018 held its grand finale on 26th May 2018 at the Dance Vision Arena, San Juan City, Philippines where Neena Macaire Bezuidenhout was crowned the first ever winner! The 21-year-old South African queen gave a spectacular performance at the finale being every bit worthy of her title.

Amidst her hectic schedule after the crowning, she finds time to talk to us in an exclusive interview where she reveals her guilty pleasure and talks about beauty pageants, her dreams, experiences in the pageant industry and more.
Q. How does it feel to win Jewel of the World 2018?

While being on stage it was an indescribable feeling of all my humbled beginnings, years of hard-work, determination and commitment all paid off in that moment. Being the First Edition Jewel of The World 2018 is such a great humbling and honorable experience all together, because to me it is more than just a title and achievement it is a life changing experience and a part of my life journey that I will cherish forever. With every opportunity that is given lies great responsibility that should be taken on with open arms. With responsibility there is empowerment to create more leaders.
I am able to use this platform to create the change that I would love to see in this world and that being said a change in all humanity’s hearts and hearts that will be united as one.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?
Never let other peoples opinions of you define who you are.
Never Give Up.
Never doubt or underestimate your inner strength and your abilities regardless of what obstacles and challenges you are faced with.
Always change negative energy and transform it into positive energy. Take criticism lightly and use it to push you towards your goals and dreams.

I believe I am a one of a kind jewel because, I have gone through processes and transformations just like a jewel needs to go through various stages and processes so too did I. It molded, shaped and transformed me into the strong woman I am today.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

I aspire to live out a purposeful and meaningful life. My inspiration comes from substance that is from within that drives me to share my dreams, hopes, truth, passions, courage and strength. I would like to be known as a beauty that serves her purpose and not just by having a beautiful face but, showing the true version of myself which resides in my heart and soul. I believe the true beauty of a woman should be reflected in her good deeds, actions, words and stay true to her humble beginnings.

Q. We all know beauty queens love to represent their country internationally, do you have any plans to participate in other major international pageants like Miss Universe or Miss World once your reign ends?

I believe every goal you set for yourself should be something that you put your all into and every achievement is a building block and step into greatness. One needs to grow and blossom into their career and once you have achieved that you can open yourself up to going big. It has always been one of my dreams and goals to participate in the Miss South Africa pageant and hopefully be elected to participate and represent at these two major platforms Miss Universe and Miss World. I hope and pray that all of my years of hard-work, dedication, commitment and passion leads me to these wonderful opportunities since it is one of my aspirations on my goal digger list.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

My life goal is to be a successful in every part of my life. I would love to be a successful business woman, owning my own Image Consultancy firm and also continue to grow my anti-bullying campaign “Never Look Back” and become a world known humanitarian.
Q. There are a lot of myths related to pageants and beauty queens. What is the one thing that you believe girls should know about holding office as a beauty queen?

A beauty queen needs to have a strong backbone, an open mind, stay true to her heart and herself. She needs to know everything there is to know about the world she lives in and be a problem solver that is able to think out of the box and on her feet. A beauty queen needs to be passionate about everything she does and have a great love to serve people in every community. She should be a beauty with a heart and use both her hands to uplift and empower every life she touches. Being a beauty queen can be tough at times especially when you live in a world where people are constantly judging you and your every move but, never let insecurities of others become insecurity to you. Always strive to aim high, do and give your best in every situation you are placed in...do not sweat the small stuff. Rather help and inspire those that criticize you and love everyone equally.
Q. Who is your idol, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I do not have one specific idol that I look up to but, instead have various idols I am inspired by. My inspiration comes from looking up to various iconic women that have shown a great amount of strength and leadership within their field. Each woman represents their own motto and stand that they took in their life which inspired many to be successful in their own right. To name a few that I am inspired by...it would be:

Princess Diana – She is a symbol of love and compassion. She served beauty with its purpose by being selfless and lived out a life dedicated to charity and the betterment of each human life. She used her platform to create change in every part of the world.

Margaret Thatcher – She was known as “The Iron Lady”, where she made an impact and influence on everyone’s life: socially, economically and culturally. She brought about change and showed true dedication. She lived up to her true status.
Marilyn Monroe – She was a symbol of femininity and embraced true beauty by not being afraid to be herself.
Coco Chanel – She was a symbol of style, simplicity and elegance. She gave woman a voice through the use of fashion.
Mother Theresa – She is a Saint and left behind her legacy to have faith, belief, love and missionaries of charity work.
Each woman is a symbol of woman empowerment and pillars of strength. They are all iconic, timeless and legendary figures to look up to and be inspired by.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I would use it as an opportunity to climb onto every airplane to travel to every part of the world. Since it is my dream and on my bucket list to see and experience the different cultures all over the world. It will be an advantage because I do not have to worry about airfare, travel allowance and luggage.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My most cherished childhood memory would be when I grew up on a farm which was where I was able to enjoy every moment of being a free-spirit, being one with nature, interacting with animals and creating a new adventure every day. I spent most of my childhood outdoors and thoroughly enjoyed playing outside looking for “fairies” in the flowers, riding on my bicycle and making mud pies. I also had my own personalized swing which was tied to one of the tallest and largest trees with rope and a huge tractor Tyre.
Q. What is your advocacy; can you tell us more about it?
You are your own brand. Your input becomes your output.

I live for the empowerment, upliftment and equal rights of every living being. My aim is to create awareness for every cause that needs a voice and platform to promote unity amongst every living being in society. I use the concept of looking beyond the surface and deep within or “Beauty is only skin deep”.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Chocolate. Dark Chocolate is one of my ultimate favorites. In actual fact, anything that looks good and tastes good.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
1) To be successful in every part of my life and achieve all the goals I set for myself.
2) To solve all problems and end world poverty, hunger and suffering. Make the world a place filled with love, peace and unity.
3) Travel over the world.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?
A. The unthinkable is always achievable.
The best advice I can give is to always stay grounded (humble) and true to your roots and yourself. ALWAYS set goals that are achievable even if it takes time or small steps at a time to reach them.
ALWAYS see the best in every outcome and take criticism to better yourself and use that negative energy as your motivation to push you into the direction you need to be in.
Live life succeeding in the passions that lies close and deep in your heart and use those passions to create a better today, tomorrow and future.
Be driven by everything that motivates, inspires and empowers you and use all of the giftings you were blessed with to do the same for someone else's life.

The ultimate goal is to be a woman with a strong mind, heart and soul and not letting anything stop her from pursuing, chasing and reaching her dreams. You are your own sailor that is in control of your sails...You decide and have the power to make the choice to live life with optimism.
Go in your destined direction, create your own platforms, aspire to inspire and most importantly live out beauty serving its purpose.

Another thing I would like to add is that I am a proud owner and founder of my own Anti-Bullying Campaign called, Never Look Back that has been running for the last 4 years (started it in 2014) where I do motivational speeches to uplift, inspire and empower the youth and people of today.
The campaign supports both the victim and perpetrator since I am a firm believer of everyone has a story to tell and we can all learn from one another and build each other up.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Universe Great Britain 2018 Finalist Romy Simpkins
dek: Miss Universe Great Britain 2018 will hold its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where thirty five beautiful divas will compete for the national title. Miss Universe Great Britain 2017 Anna Burdzy will crown her successor at the end of the event finale. The…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Universe Great Britain 2018 Finalist Romy Simpkins
paragraphs: Miss Universe Great Britain 2018 will hold its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where thirty five beautiful divas will compete for the national title. Miss Universe Great Britain 2017 Anna Burdzy will crown her successor at the end of the event finale. The winner of the national pageant will represent her country at Miss Universe 2018.

But before that, here we have one of the finalist, Romy Simpkins, in a candid and exclusive interview with Angelopedia where she answers everything from her dreams and ambitions to her guilty pleasures and goals.
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Universe Great Britain 2018?

I am over the moon to be making a comeback to Miss Universe Great Britain after competing in the 2012 finals, which was my very first pageant. I am mentally and physically prepared to walk the Miss Universe Great Britain stage in hope of representing the nation at Miss Universe.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?

Honestly, learning to just be myself. I believe I have become the strong, confident and ambition women I am today by simply being me. There no need to fake things, if you want to be accepted by other you at first must accept yourself which I do. I am proud of what I have achieved throughout my life and to be able to say makes me realise how important my life is.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

Following on from having self- acceptance, it’s about knowing you can make a difference to otherpeople’s lives as I did my own. I struggled as a teenager with my body image, but I look back now and despite the hard times I faced. If that hadn’t challenged me, I wouldn’t be who I am or where I am today. Being that someone to a person may look up to is so rewarding and now I can even go on to say I am working in a sector that supports people with mental health issues. This is something I personally dealt with and defeated and now I want to help others to fight it too. Being the best version of myself, allows other to see you don’t need to be perfect. There no such things as the ideal body shape, but simply learning to love yourself and treating your body as your temple inspires me to keep going.
Q. You have also held the prestigious title of Miss International UK 2016, tell us a little about how that changed your life?

It was an incredible experience getting to compete in one of the big four pageant in the world. I will be forever blessed to have the opportunity to compete in Japan and to meet ladies from different backgrounds and cultures, it was a breath of fresh air! It allowed me to make friendship with people I would never had met if it wasn’t for Miss International and the organisation. My chaperone from Miss Internationalwho was like a stand in Mum and I still email one another to see which country we are visiting next in hope of bumping into one another. It made me realiseI can do anything I set my mind to, but by working hard, being dedicated and passionate about pageantry has given me an amazing outlook on life and to make the most of every day.
Q. Other than the Miss Universe Great Britain crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?

It’s not about the crown or the sash but the opportunity to represent women in my country and around the world as an individual who believes in herself. I have always been a goal setter and will always push myself in fulfilling aspiration and reaching my ambitions. I want to be the voice for others who may not feel they can have one, as I want them to know that they are the one in control of theirlife and they can have the best life ever by simply focusing on their dreams and making them a reality.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

Miss Universe Great Britain is a large milestone in my life, I’m pushing myself into somethingI have always wanted since the beginning of my pageant journey. I’ve worked my way up to show I am capable of being successful and my life goal is to be successful in what I do. That goes for anything, no matter what the results If I know I have done my best in everything, I feel I have accomplished my life goal of being a successful woman.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Universe Great Britain 2018?

I’d like to represent myself at Miss Universe Great Britaina fierce, resilient and positive young woman. I want to show that this competition is a big challenge, but it is exciting as I look forward to making amazing friendships during the final.
Q. Do you think the fact that you are already a pageant queen will play as a major advantage in your favour?

I wouldn’t say it’s an advantage as every pageant is very different, with what they expect from contestants and of course their winner. However, I feel I have proven to myself that I can represent Great Britain with upmost pride at Miss Universe, by knowing I have worked may up towards this title after competing internationally twice. Those opportunities weren’t just handed to me, I put my all into them and the reward for that was being able to go to internationals. Both internationals were incredible, and I would do them 100 times over again. But it shows I am strong minded and can handle being in an intense competition which I know Miss Universe is and I would be so honored to have that once in a life time experience to take it on!
Q. Who is your idol, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

So, I don’t have an idol. I have two! My Mum and Dad are my idols, they are my biggest supporters and I admire how much they really believe in me. They’ve always taught me that if you work hard you will get where you want to be and that’s probably why I am the way I am, in the sense of driven. Both my Mum and Dad both run their own businesses and I find that inspiring, it has pushed me to do the same as I launch my bespoke swimwear range last year. I feel a lot of the morals they have taught me, I stand for already. We are a close family and I am so lucky to have that, and I hope to spread the importance of looking after those nearest and dearest to you, both family members and friends. They will always be the ones to catch up when you fall, and you will be there to do the same for them and I am so grateful to have them in my life. I hope to teach the next generation to be ambition, be confident in your ability and never give up on the things you don’t go a day without thinking about.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

You may find this a bit random, but that’s me really! If I could be invisible I would love to watch and see where my two cats go when they leave the house for adventures. Especially at night, of course if I’m just casually walking behind them they may not go anywhere but if I was invisible I’d love to see what they get up to. They always come back looking like they’ve eaten for two and smell like perfume. I always imagine them having cat parties with the other cats in the neighborhood, theynever fail to amuse me!
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

I have had many wonderful memories growing up, so it is really hard to narrow it down. My favorite times were being on stage and as a child I spent a lot of time performing in shows. So, I would say a very special memory was when I auditions for The Arts Educational School at the age of 13, most of the children who auditioned had a musical instrument of some sort to play. But as I didn’t play one, I was asked to do something else to show why I deserved a place. I decided to perform an acting monologue from the play A Midsummer Night’s Dream as I love Shakespeare. I remember clear as day performing it and the room was just silent afterwards, I smiled and walked out. Although that may have felt uncomfortable for some, I knew with a quiet confidence that I had won my place in the school to which I was then called a few days later offering a place to start in the new school year. I still can remember my piece over 10 years later and have even used it as apart of my talent piece in pageants.
Q. What is your advocacy, can you tell us more about it?

My advocacy is mental health, I am ambassador for my MIND mental health charity in my local area. I attend fortnightly support and well-being groups to help talk and address people issues of anxiety, depression and other conditions they may have. I have supported this cause for many years as it’s something personal and close to my heart. Mental Health can be a hidden illness which is just as dangerous as someone with a physical impairment or disability and can result in someone quality of life being seriously affected. I have completed a course on mental health and am studying to become a trained therapist. I wish to use this platform to set up my own support groups for young people who are suffering with eating disorders and to form my own charity to provide better access to therapy and support for these people, so they can be treated quicker and in the right way for their complex conditions. I look forward to gaining more professional knowledge, hands on experience after qualifying as a psychodynamic counselor in the field of childhood trauma and eating disorders.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
I know I am not the only one who has this, but I have avery naughty sweet tooth. I love chocolate, kinder is my favorite and that’s all I can say really!
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

A big thing I would wish for is having equal rights between men and women in all areas of life, this is anissue that needs to change as I believe we should always feel equal to those around us. I wish that there was a cure for dementia. It’s a condition that is in-reversable and can have such a big impact on how someone with the condition can live. As well as this the impact it has on the people around that person can be very heartbreaking. My final wish would be to let every person in the world, who may feel alone or unable to speak about there issues or conditions. To know they really aren’t alone and to make them realise that most people in today’s society have experienced or have been faced with some form of mental health and it can be controlled and stopped with the right support and guidance. But most importantly with that is wishing people would be more open to listening to those in their time of need.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans atAngelopedia?

I just wanted to say a massive thank you to everyone who has ever supported me in my pageant journey. The words of wisdom and positivity have been over whelming and I am so grateful to be apart of a community that thrives of empowering others.
Thank you and I won’t let you down!
Miss International UK 2016

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Missouri Earth United States 2018 Chrystelle Volckmann
dek: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Missouri Earth United States 2018 Chrystelle Volckmann
paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss Missouri Earth United States 2018 Chrystelle Volckmann sharing her experience and journey of being the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q . How does it feel to be the winner of Miss Missouri Earth United States 2018 and a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

It honestly has been such a blessing to be a part of an organization that stands for something so powerful. I was born and raised in Missouri, and now am continuing my education here in Missouri, so being given the honor to represent my state has already been such a wonderful experience. I truly feel like this has been such a great opportunity and I couldn't be more excited for meeting all of the other delegates and having the chance to compete next month.
Q . What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

The best lesson that I have learned so far in my journey as a delegate for Miss Earth United States is it's important to keep the end goal in mind, but also to relax, have fun, and realize the purpose of the organization. We are all "beauty with a cause" and what I, as well as all of the other delegates, really want to accomplish is making a positive difference on this earth.
Q . What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

When I was younger, I was in a severe car accident that nearly took my life. This experience has made me so grateful to just be alive each and everyday. I vowed to myself earlier on to always keep enduring and to live my best life possible/be the best version of myself each and every day, because you never know when it can be taken from you.
Q . We would love to know more about your advocacy to save the Planet Earth and what drove you to choose it?

My advocacy to help save the Planet Earth is wildlife conservation/health care. I grew up on a farm, and spent a lot of time out in nature. I helped my dad care for all of the animals on the farm, and this created a huge love from animals in me. I am currently in my senior year of studying animal science, and I am applying for Veterinary college this fall. With my love and passion for animal care, advocating for wildlife conservation/health care was a natural drive for me. I had the incredible honor of getting to go to South Africa in May/June this year to work a a veterinary outrach group where we helped provide animal care to communities in need.
Q . How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage of Miss Earth United States 2018?

On the national stage of Miss Earth United States, I would love to represent myself as someone confident, ready for the job, and classy. I hope my presence on the stage portrays this and that the judges get a good opportunity of learning who I am during the interview.
Q . Who is your idol, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I would have to say that one of my idols would have to Audrey Hepburn. Not only was she able to become this image representative of class and pose, but she stood for something greater than herself. She had such huge involvement with UNICEF and other humanitarian organizations. When a person is blessed with that much influence in the world, I find it extremely important in being a good role model to stand for others and give back.
Q . If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

If I was invisible for a day, I would travel as much as possible. I mean, really think about it, trains or planes, they would all be accessible for the day. I would definitely try and go see everything I could fit into one day.
Q . Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

One of my most special childhood memories would have to be when my family would take the boat out on the lake and we would could "tubing". I always loved trying to hang on while the tube was going really fast and my dad would try to turn the boat quickly trying to throw me off. We would stay out on the lake all day, and eat our packed lunches right out on the boat. Sometimes my dad would go fishing, while my mom and me went swimming or just layed out in the sun.
Q . What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

Honestly, I would have to say my Dad has helped empower to be who I am each and every day. I was adopted by the man I call Dad when I was 8 years old, and he has made one of the biggest impacts on my life possible. Everytime I need advice, or just a good laugh to get through, he is always there and I believe that I am the strong person I am today, because of all of the support I get from him and my family.
Q . What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

My guilty pleasure would definitely have to be bubble tea. I spent some time in LA my freshmen year and some of my friends down there introduced me to bubble tea. It has definitely been my guilty pleasure ever since. Whenever I am feeling down or just a little bit stressed out, I treat myself to strawberry shortcake bubble tea.
Q . We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

Like I said before, being given the opportunity to competed for the title of Miss Earth United States is just a blessing in itself. Ultimately, I would just like to be proud of my performance and know that I made a positive difference in someone or something's life. I am also really looking forward to meeting all of the incredible women from across the country and I hope to develop lifelong friendships.
Q . If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

If I were granted 3 wishes, my first wish would be to get rid of animal cruelty. I would next wish for all of my family to be cared/provided for and to be happy. Lastly, I would wish for the world to be a more understanding and less selfish place.
Q . Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

Remember that change starts with you. Think of every dollar that you spend as your vote for what our market desires. Educate yourself on the things you believe in and always stay true to who you are. Enjoy each and every day because you never know when it will be your last.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Grand Australia 2018 Kimberly Gundani
dek: Kimberly Gundani was crowned Miss Grand Australia 2018 at the grand finale held on 16th June 2018. She is now going to represent her country at Miss Grand International 2018. To have achieved such an honor and appreciation from her followers and supporters…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Grand Australia 2018 Kimberly Gundani
paragraphs: Kimberly Gundani was crowned Miss Grand Australia 2018 at the grand finale held on 16th June 2018. She is now going to represent her country at Miss Grand International 2018. To have achieved such an honor and appreciation from her followers and supporters, Kimberly still remains grounded and humble.
In an exclusive interview with Angelopedia, Kimberly talks about her responsibilities being a national title holder, her childhood, dreams and ambitions of her life.
Q . How does it feel to be crowned Miss Grand Australia 2018 and now a delegate of Miss Grand International 2018?

I am so humbled and honoured to be Miss Grand Australia and a delegate for Miss Grand International 2018. To be the first black African-Australian to win an international pageant in Australia is just incredible and a true honour.
Q . What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Grand Australia 2018?

Through hard work, resilience and a heart of service, anything is possible. I love to reach out to my community. Miss Grand Australia helped to raise awareness about domestic violence in our stop the war and violence campaign. The response was phenomenal.
Q . What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

I’m driven to achieve my goals because I know that there is so much work to be done in our fight against domestic violence and war. Until every woman, child and community are safe, I will always try my best to better myself in order to help others.
Q . As a student of Masters in Law, How do you think that your education will benefit you in fulfilling your ambition?

I discovered my voice when I started my Master of Law Juris Doctor program. When you have something to give to the world, you should never be afraid to use it in order to give back. My education has helped me and will continue to help me to advocate for women and children in order to stop war and violence.
Q . How would you like to represent yourself at the international stage of Miss Grand International 2018?

As a representative of Australia, I embody our values of unity, kindness and hard work. I endeavor to represent our country and its diversity at Miss Grand Internationalupholding Australian values at all times. We are a progressive people and Miss Grand Australia has been the perfect platform to represent that aspect of our identity.
Q . Who is your ideal, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

Barack Obama. In the face to negativity regarding his race, education and background, he rose above it all. He was graceful and kind in his presidency and continues to hold himself to a high standard. The next generation can learn a lot from him as he showcases that through adversity and hardship, you can still achieve your goals and inspire other young people.
Q . If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
I would travel across as many boarders as possible. I love going to new places and I’m very adventurous.
Q . Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

Christmas time with my grandmother was the most memorable and most special childhood memory that I cling to. My grandmother would prepare her Christmas tree and decorate it with balls of cotton wool to resemble snow.My grandmother would bake cakes wearing her yellow apron and the smell of the baking would fill the whole house. The sun would stream into the kitchen and there was a cool summer breeze. It was a time for family, warmth and laughter. The last time I saw grandmother before she passed away, she gave me her yellow apron which I continue to treasure and is a daily reminder of her love, compassionand care for others.
Q . What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard everyday?

My mother is my inspiration. I live in a single parent household and she has fought to better my future. My mother has sacrificed a lot, by leaving Zimbabwe, moving to England and then Australia; she is resilient and empowered but also kind and gentle. My mother is selfless and endeavors to support those in need to the best of her ability. To me, she embodies true beauty and if I can be a quarter of the woman she is, I would have done a good job.
Q . What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Coffee is definitely my guilty pleasure. I live in Melbourne and we have a very strong coffee culture.
Q . We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

My aim is to have a positive impact in Australia and the world by advocating for women and children affected by domestic violence. Miss Grand Australia is an incredible platform to break barriers and bring taboo subjects into the light. Together we can make sure that every person who experiences domestic violence is heard and knows that we do not accept violence and war and this starts in the home.
Q . If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
The first wish would be to end domestic violence against women and children, achieving a healthy lifestyle for all and being the first black African-Australian to be Miss Grand International.
Q . Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

This crown and title represents all of us and it unites us. We are all different and unique and this should be celebrated. Thank you for being so kind and gracious and welcoming me into the Miss Grand International family.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss North Carolina Earth United States 2018 Madison McGee
dek: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss North Carolina Earth United States 2018 Madison McGee
paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss North Carolina Earth United States 2018 Madison McGee sharing her experience and journey of becoming the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
1. How does it feel to be the winner of Miss North Carolina Earth United States 2018 and a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I feel so incredibly blessed to be Miss North Carolina Earth 2018. I am honored as a collegiate soccer player to represent athletic women all across the country on the Miss Earth United States stage in July. To say I am excited for this amazing opportunity would be an understatement!
2. What is the best lesson you’ve learned in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

The best lesson I have learned in my journey so far as Miss North Carolina Earth 2018 is that actions do matter. When I spoke to fifth graders about the importance of recycling, I had a boy ask me if it really made a difference whether he recycled and took actions to keep our Earth clean since he was only in fifth grade. My answer was yes because even if we only have one fifth grade boy taking action, it is bound to start a chain reaction in others. Everyone’s actions contribute to something so much greater than ourselves.
3. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

One thing that inspires me to be the best version of myself would definitely be my family. They have always supported me in everything that I have done in my life, and I would not be where I am today without them. I am so grateful to have been blessed with the best family ever.
4. We would love to know more about your advocacy to save the Planet Earth and what drove you to choose it?

My advocacy is “Plant the seeds, Save the trees.” I focus on replenishing the trees in the environment because while trees give us many important resources like paper for books and lumber for homes, it is so important to make sure we put back what we take. I not only want to plant tree seedlings, but I want to plant seeds of encouragement in people about environmental issues. I hope that those people will then plant seeds of encouragement in people that they meet, and we will have hundreds of new Earth warriors! I chose this platform because I grew up playing soccer outside and developed an appreciation for shade trees on hot, sunny days. There never seemed to be enough at parks.
5. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage of Miss Earth United States 2018?
I would like to represent myself gracefully on the Miss Earth United States stage. I hope that my dedication and passion for making a difference for the Earth will shine.
6. Who is your ideal, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life and teach the next generation?

My idol would have to be my late grandma, Sandy McGee. She was always able to find the humor in any situation and accepted people for who they truly were. My grandmother found the joy in every obstacle that life threw her way. I hope that I can inculcate her kindness and compassion for people into my own life. Also, I hope to teach the next generation to always find the joy and humor in life despite the trials they may face, just like my grandmother did.
7. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
If I could be invisible for a day, I would definitely take a rocket to the moon. Only a handful of people get to see Earth from space, and I think it would be absolutely amazing.
8. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My most special childhood memory would have to be making homemade macaroni and cheese with my grandmother. She would let me stand on a stool at the stove with her and stir the macaroni until I got tired. She was so patient with me. It is a favorite memory of mine because she taught me at a very young age how to cook and who doesn’t love macaroni and cheese!
9. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

My parents and family empower me to be myself and work hard every day. They encourage me to be my absolute best no matter what the task, and I could never thank them enough. Through their constant support in good times and bad, I was able to pursue my goal of playing collegiate soccer. I wouldn’t be where I am today without my parents and siblings, and I seek to make them proud.
10. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
My guilty pleasure would definitely be chocolate ice cream. I could eat chocolate ice cream every day!
11. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

One thing I ultimately want to achieve from the pageant is to grow as a person and make new friends. Outside of the pageant, I want to graduate college with a degree in Accounting and start working my way up to being a CEO of a major bank. I want to live a life that I can look back on and have no regrets.
12. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
If I had 3 wishes, I would first wish for a cure for cancer. Then, I would wish for the ability to read people’s minds. My third wish would be to end world hunger.
13. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

I would like to first thank Angelopedia for giving me this opportunity. My message to fans would be to have the courage to pursue new adventures that push you out of your comfort zone. It is when you are pushed out of your comfort zone that you grow into the person you are meant to be!

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Michigan Earth United States 2018 Jasmina Cunmulaj
dek: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Michigan Earth United States 2018 Jasmina Cunmulaj
paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss Michigan Earth United States 2018 Jasmina Cunmulaj sharing her experience and journey of being the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q. How does it feel to be the winner of Miss Michigan Earth United States 2018 and a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?
I feel so grateful for this opportunity to represent Michigan at Miss Earth United States. Knowing that this pageant has such a genuinely wholesome and driven purpose is what makes me so proud!
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I have learned that being myself is the best lesson. In this journey of life in general, we need to find out who we are born to be, and embrace that with all of our hearts. This past year has been an eye opening experience for me as I have been blessed with this opportunity to be Miss Michigan Earth United States. In the end, what matters is that we lived our lives to our fullest potential, being completely ourselves.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

Everyday I have to take a moment to realize how lucky I am to be doing the things I do. From being able to have a college education, to representing Michigan, and basic things like even having water to drink or a roof over my head. The people out there who do not have these things are what inspire me to keep going and be the best version of myself. I know that not everyone has these opportunities, and so with that, I would like to ensure that I become an advocate for those who cannot speak up and fight for themselves for a better life. My motivation has become the young girls and boys of this world.
Q. We would love to know more about your advocacy to save the Planet Earth and what drove you to choose it?

This has been one of the most exciting years of my life, thus far. Being able to have my own non-profit organization has been such a wonderful experience and privilege. My advocacy is a non-profit called The Flower Girls (www.theflowergirls.org) and it aims to inspire the female youth of today to go out into this world and be advocates for change for the Earth itself. Through the organization, we have monthly meetings with the young girls to participate in green-clean-ups, education about the environment and ways to fight back against climate change. Also, we have other female role models who play an important part in being eco-friendly come in and speak to our girls. My mission is to not only inspire these young girls to make a difference within the environment, but to make a difference within their generation and generations to come, with confidence, poise, and a passion to help the world we live in.

I decided to use this as my advocacy because as a Developmental Psychology major in school, I knew that my love for children could not be subsided. I wanted to truly find a way to make a large impact on the environment, and the young girls today. It takes mankind to fix what mankind has destroyed, so we need to start with our youth to lead this change.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I would like to represent myself as a young woman who is full of genuine intention to make a difference. At the conclusion of MEUS, I want to be the woman that all young girls can look up to and say “I want to be like her when I grow up!” Because when I know I have reached and inspired a young girl in that way, then I have truly won.
Q. Who is your ideal, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I would like to choose two or three…but all have essentially stemmed from one, which would be my Mother. Coming from former war-torn Yugoslavia, my Mother has exemplified all things a strong woman carries. She, aside from her actual outer beauty, is one of the most respected, loving and kind women I am so lucky to know and have as a Mother. The two people I mentioned prior would be the late Princess Diana, and Saint Mother Teresa. Growing up, my Mother has taken traits from them, such as philanthropic motives, compassion, and love. I am so grateful for my Mother introducing me to the values and qualities of these role models. I hope to carry those traits and qualities from all three for the rest of my life, and pass them down to future generations.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I would love to travel everywhere and hop from flight to flight! There are so many places I want to see in this world, and with my busy schedule lately I haven’t had the time to be able to visit them! So with that invisibility for a day, I would take advantage of that and travel!
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

Many of my childhood memories come from being outdoors, since I spent a majority of my childhood summers back home in Montenegro. I would say riding horses in an open field as a young girl with my best friend Sarah is something I will always cherish to this day. There is nothing more in this world that I love than being on a horses back in a field that stretches so far beyond view. Life as an adult gets filled with responsibilities (good ones), and we take our free and precious youthful times for granted.
Q. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard everyday?

My Mother is my biggest inspiration and empowers me in so many ways. She constantly keeps me grounded and humble, but also knows what to say to get me focused and motivated. I know that she has sacrificed a great deal of her life for me to get this far, so making her proud is the least I could do in return.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

I am known in my family for cooking and baking, but also known for loving to eat healthy. So when I do find a bit of spare time, I am always finding new recipes to make and test out. My guilty pleasure steps in when those recipes are desserts…especially pie. I blame this on my European roots!
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

I ultimately want to be a human rights activist and make a genuine, impactful change for children and women. Those two specific areas may seem to receive a lot of attention, but numbers and statistics do not match up to that attention and are frequently much lower. I want to take my passion, education, and motivation and combine those qualities to ultimately achieve success, not for myself, but for all those who are in dire need. If there is one thing I have learned in this life, it is that we need to always put others before ourselves. When we do that, the happiness and relief from those people becomes our true success in return.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
1) World Peace 2) The end to Climate Change 3) A garden with endless white roses and hydrangeas
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

Thank you so much for taking the time to interview me and also share my story! The message for the fans of Angelopedia I would like to leave you all with would be to find your passion in life, and use it to motivate you in everything you do. The Flower Girls is my passion, and that has become the motivation and future goal that leads me to do everything I do! Use your voice and your heart, and your thoughts and actions will not be unheard nor unseen. In the end, what matters is that you did what you were driven to do with full force (as long as you do not hurt others in the process) and you feel complete in your heart. You never know how your courage and passion can change others, too!

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Colorado Earth United States 2018 Bre L’Estrange
dek: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Colorado Earth United States 2018 Bre L’Estrange
paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss Colorado Earth United States 2018 Bre L’Estrange sharing her experience and journey of being the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q. How does it feel to be the winner of Miss Colorado Earth United States 2018 and a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

It is such an honor. Ever since I was a little girl I have always wanted to make a change while empowering others to follow their dreams. It’s surreal to think that I will be competing at Miss Earth United States in just a little under two months while advocating for environmental awareness and being a beauty for a cause.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

Consistency is key, passion is essential. Staying consistent with raising awareness for our environment is so important whether that is recycling, using stainless steel straws, or growing your own ecosystem. All of these things are small actions that can make a huge impact on our Earth. Taking action is a huge part but never losing hope and staying passionate about these issues is essential. Making connections with others as well as taking action to make a change and spread environmental awareness is the perfect formula for positive change.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

First and foremost, my loved ones. I would not be where I am today without my family and their constant support. My mom is my biggest inspiration because she has not only taught me how to be a strong, independent woman but to give back in any way I can while having a voice for things that matter. My boyfriend is a huge part of my journey and life, he is my biggest supporter and never goes a day without encouraging me and letting me know how proud he is of me. I am inspired every single day to be the best version of myself not only for my loved ones and others but for me.
Q. We would love to know more about your advocacy to save the Planet Earth and what drove you to choose it?

I was born and raised in a small town, Glenwood Springs, Colorado. This town is located and surrounded by beautiful mountains, lakes, and the best hiking trails you can imagine. Taking steps to save our planet and appreciate the environment has always been a part of my life. My main advocacy to save our Planet Earth, stemmed from my favorite hiking spot called “Hanging Lake.” Hanging Lake is a unique crystal blue lake that sits at the bottom of a waterfall where locals and tourists take an hour-long hike to get to. Recently my town has had to take certain precautions and actions towards preserving hanging lake because of the increase of heavy foot traffic and water quality within visiting the trail every day. This place is a part of my heart and I am going to do everything I can to raise awareness for this issue as well as many environmental issues going on today.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I would like to represent myself at Miss Earth United States by showing the contestants and judges my 100% unapologetic self. I want to be viewed as a strong, independent, empowering woman who has a voice and uses it for positive change within our environment. It is an honor to be Miss Colorado Earth and I want to be able to not only pass down the legacy of the Miss Earth Org. but create my own in the process.
Q. Who is your ideal, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

My Idol would have to be all of the strong women of this world (specifically my mom). I feel women empowerment and equality is on the rise and I want to be able to be a voice in this journey. In my life, I have always strived for empowerment within myself and others, so what I hope to do is teach the younger generations to empower one another and understand that we are all equal. Each person has a dream, a goal, a passion and if all of us continue to come together and make a positive change who knows what this world is capable of.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

If I could be invisible for a day I would use it to go to children’s hospitals all across the world. Environmental awareness is a huge platform of mine, but I am also very involved with Love Your Melon which helps fund and raises awareness for pediatric cancer research. I would want to collect as much information as possible on this issue and help further the process to one day find a cure for cancer. My grandmother struggled with cancer twice and is a two-time survivor, she was my main inspiration to start volunteering and spending time in the field. So, to have the ability to be invisible I would use it to my advantage to seek out information that would not be easy to come by if I were visible.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My most special childhood memory would be when my mom and I would decorate our house for every holiday. Whether that was Christmas, Halloween, Easter, even St. Patrick’s Day. Celebrating is a huge part of my life and I am so grateful for all the countless memories and blessings I have in my life.
Q. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

What empowers me every day to be myself and work hard are my dreams. I have a dream journal where I write all of my goal and aspirations in life. This helps me not only observe things I need to improve on but how I can reach my goals. I want to be able to look back and say I was the woman, me as a little girl wanted to be.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

Netflix and In-and-out. I am a major homebody even though I love eating healthy and working out, my guilty pleasure would have to be staying home in my PJs binge watching my favorite show while eating a cheeseburger (and of course animal fries).
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?
I want to achieve growth. Whether that is within this platform or myself, I want to walk away from this competition feeling satisfied and content with how I not only represented Colorado but myself.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
I would wish to win the title of Miss Earth United States, eternal health & happiness for my family, and for three more wishes to devote to climate change, pollution, and toxicity of marine life.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

Be Yourself. No one is as authentic and unique as you are. We live in a world full of certain “labels” and “standards” but really the biggest standard you should have is how hard can you work for your dream; how much you can push yourself to succeed and how much change you can make. We are all in this together! Thank you Angelopedia fans and your support, if you have a dream go chase it. You can achieve anything you set your mind to.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Kansas Earth United States 2018 McKenzie Hersh
dek: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Kansas Earth United States 2018 McKenzie Hersh
paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss Kansas Earth United States 2018 McKenzie Hersh sharing her experience and journey of being the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q. How does it feel to be the winner of Miss Kansas Earth United States 2018 and a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

Simply put, it feels astonishing. I am so excited to represent my home state, Kansas, in the Miss Earth United States Pageant 2018. All of the other delegates for Miss Earth United States 2018 that I have had the pleasure of meeting, are such incredible women, and to be able to represent the state of Kansas by their sides is such an honor. I couldn’t have asked for a better group of women to experience this ride with.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

The best lesson I have learned in my journey as a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 is how to better serve our Mother Earth and how to inspire others to follow suit. Before my delegacy I did not know all the different ways that I could make a difference in helping to clean our Earth. I had the pleasure of participating in an event put on by The Green Prom Movement. This organization takes used prom dresses, renovates them and holds several events across the Kansas City metropolitan area where girls can come and receive these beautiful dresses for their big night. What they may not know, is that in doing so they have helped to cut down on what is commonly known as “fast fashion.” Fast fashion is mass producing clothing that is up to the newest fashion trend, and in doing so they drive the prices of these items down. With the prices being so low, you may not worry about throwing something away to justify getting the newest trend. “Fast Fashion” is the cause of more than 15 million tons of textile waste. The Green Prom Movement is doing their part in helping to stop the waste of perfectly good dresses. It feels so good to have had the chance to be a part of such a noble movement.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

My support system is the one thing I give the most credit to inspiring me to be the best version of myself. I have such amazing people in my life that support and push me to try new things and to better myself in any way I can.
Q. We would love to know more about your advocacy to save the Planet Earth and what drove you to choose it?

My advocacy to save the Planet Earth is all about reducing our carbon footprint so that future generations can live cleaner and healthier lives. We burn fossil fuels, non-renewable energy sources, any time we turn on our cars, run the heat to our homes, and use electricity on anything as simple as a light. The state of Kansas helps reducing its carbon footprint by setting up a series of windmills throughout western Kansas. I have started to do my part by building a tiny home to live in. The reduction of space for living drops the amount of energy used for cooling by nearly fourteen times. This is the best way I can see to quickly reduce my footprint and to live a cleaner life. I am a huge advocate to living tiny because of the benefits it has on our environment, even though I have to compromise on closet space. It is a small price to pay to live a life that has a smaller impact on our beautiful Mother Earth.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I want to represent myself as a strong, confidently beautiful, and Earth conscious woman. Representing my state is such a great opportunity to show who I am and how I can make a difference in helping to make our Earth a cleaner and safer place to live for us, and for generations to come.
Q. Who is your idol, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

My idol is Sarah Thomas. Sarah was the first female referee to officiate an NFL game. She smashed the barrier of an all-male officiated league. Her values allowed her to overcome the odds and never give up to make it to the highest level of her field. I wish to instill these values to myself and teach them to the next generation. No matter what obstacles lay in your way, always give it all you have to make your dreams come true.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

If I was invisible for a day I would spend the first part of the day driving my car around to scare people that there is a car rolling around with no driver. The next part of the day I would want to stand by manikins and talk to people as they walk by to see if they would talk back to the manikin. And the last part of the day, I would go up on top of the tallest building in Kansas City and watch the sunset.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My most special memory wasn’t necessarily during my childhood but was when my childhood dream came true. That was when I signed my Letter of Intent to play softball at the college level. It was special to me because all of the long practices, and weekends that I sacrificed throughout my adolescence paid off.
Q. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard everyday?

My morals are the thing that empowers me to be myself and work hard every day. I believe that you must push yourself to be a better version of yourself. I try to out work myself from day to day. That is a lesson that all people should learn, it doesn’t matter what other people think about you as long as you are true to who you are always give your best.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

I pride myself in working very hard, giving my best each and every day. That being said, my guilty pleasure would be sleeping in. When I get a day off from the twelve hour shifts at the hospital and from school, I may have other things to do, but given the time to sleep in and lounge around allows me to become refreshed and ready for the next busy day that I am given.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?
My ultimate goal is to live ahappy and healthy so that I can enjoy life to the fullest of my ability.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

My first wish would be having the ability to make my hair do what I want, when I want. All girls know the frustration of spending hours trying to make their hair perfect, but it not turning out exactly how they want. Also, being able to have long hair one day and short hair another would be the ultimate paradise. My second wish would bethe ability to learn, retain and apply any knowledge learned through any media source I touch. Lastly, to be able to eat whatever I want, whenever I want, for the rest of my life with no ill effects.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

The message that I would like to give to the fans of Angelopedia is that every time we talk to someone we leave an impression on that person that can either be positive or negative. When we talk to people our mission should be to leave a lasting and positive impression. This is challenging because sometimes you may not be feeling well, or you are just having a rough day, but the person you may be speaking to could be in the same boat. You may be able to change the direction of their day by being positive even though you aren’t feeling your best. Being able to possibly affect someone’s life in a positive way is more than enough reason to take a positive approach to everything in life that we take on.
