title: Beauty Talks with Miss Nebraska Earth United States 2018 Merrick Randy Alexander
dek: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Nebraska Earth United States 2018 Merrick Randy Alexander
paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss Nebraska Earth United States 2018 Merrick Randy Alexander sharing her experience and journey of being the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q. How does it feel to be the winner of Miss NebraskaEarth United States 2018 and a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I feel humbled beyond belief to hold this title and represent such a selfless organization. Never in my wildest dreams did I think I would be in this position representing the beautiful state of Nebraska, and hopefully the USA. I have been greeted with endless support and kindness, which has overwhelmed my heart with love and warmth. I am truly so grateful, and will do everything in my power to honor this title.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I have learned the importance of community and that it truly takes a village. Wearing this crown in not about me at all, it is about all of the incredible people I get to help, and about preserving and protecting the gift God gave us all, Earth. So often people see themselves as the center of their world, but holding this title has taught me that I am a part of something so much bigger than myself. It isawe-inspiring to me to see what my work in the community does for those around me and for generations to come. We can all make a difference because even one tiny pebble can make a ripple.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

One source of inspiration to me is my faith. God is with me through each step, and it consumes me with joy to know that I am walking the path he planned for me. Other sources of inspiration are the smiles upon the faces of each person I encounter. I want to make a difference in the lives of those around me. I want to help make their lives easier and more beautiful and healthy in any way I can. The support, encouragement, and love I receive makes me want to be my best self, and give back as much as I am able to the people who have given me everything I could ever possibly need and want. And I do not mean material things, but instead things like, love, encouragement, and a sense of belonging. The opportunity to be Miss Nebraska Earth 2018 is one of a kind, and has provided deeper meaning to each day.
Q. We would love to know more about your advocacy to save the Planet Earth and what drove you to choose it?

First of all, my advocacy is to preserve and protect Earth. Earth is truly a gift, and has been taken advantage of for hundreds of years. It is up to us now to work on changing our behavior and working to cleanse the Earth of garbage and damage. These changes will not happen overnight, but the more awareness we spread about recycling, picking up trash, reusable straws, bags, and cups, plant diversity, etc. we can begin to cause multiple ripples and then hopefully a wave of change. Let’s be the difference our Earth needs and the people of Earth need.

My personal platform is “You Define You.” I came up with this movement to teach men and women all over the world that their circumstances do not have to define them. This is a movement to become extraordinary. We need to dare to dream bigger than we have ever dreamt before, and have the courage to pursue those dreams. We can break out of whatever box we are placed into, either by ourselves or by others, and become the incredible person we are meant to be. It begins with believing in yourself, and recognizing that you are capable of achieving whatever it is that your heart desires. Make the changes necessary and chase after your dreams and goals. Believe in yourself; I believe in you.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage of Miss Earth United States 2018?

I plan to represent myself as genuine, imperfect, compassionate, and selfless. I want to show people it is okay to be goofy, it is okay to recognize that we do have flaws and that we have made mistakes. I want to be a role model that is approachable. I never want people to think that I am above them or better than them because we are all incredible, wonderful, AMAZING children of God. I do not rank above any other person, and will never behave as though I do. I will represent myself as someone with empathy and intelligence. My goal is to make at least one person smile each day, and make sure each person I meet feels loved, cared for, and comfortable. I hope to represent myself and Nebraska with kindness, grace, and poise on the National stage, and truly just live in the moment appreciating all the blessings the Miss Earth United States Organization has brought to my life.
Q. Who is your ideal, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I am thankful because there are many people in my life that influence my values in such a positive way, and I hope I can take my favorite aspects of each of their lives and instill it in myself and others. My parents have taught me to dream, and have shown me how to work hard to achieve those dreams. They are so giving of their time and of their energy, and I am grateful to them for being with me through everything life has thrown at me. Connie Barnes, my mother’s bestfriend, is the most courageous woman I know. She has now successfully beat two forms of cancer with nothing but a smile on her face. I hope I can face trials with that same strength and poise. Kaylee Carlberg has taught me what it means to be Miss Nebraska Earth, and I hope to have as selfless a heart as she does someday. God is the biggest influence on my values. He has taught me to love unconditionally and provide for others in any way I am capable.I believe that values are best shown through our actions, and I hope through my actions I can teach the next generation to be strong, kind-hearted, courageous, selfless, understanding, empathetic, generous, and honest. These, among others, are some of the values that mean the most to me, and I believe will make a huge difference in our world.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I probably wouldn’t sunbathe because I don’t know if the sun actually would affect an invisible person! I would spend the day doing the things I love like dancing because I could dance anywhere at any time without people seeing me! I may play some innocent pranks on good friends because how could you miss that prime opportunity to be goofy in disguise? However, I do think it is important, invisible or not, to maintain high morals and good character at all times.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

All of my most special childhood memories involve my family. I grew up on a farm outside of a small town in Nebraska, and there was one harsh winter where we had a big snow and ice storm. Our powerlines were down for at least two weeks, and we had to run strictly off of a generator or use candles and flashlights. We began to run low on food, and could not drive to town because of the immense amount of snow and ice, so my older brother and I decided to make it fun! We got out our snow mobile, bundled up, and drove over all the massive drifts all the way to town to buy milk and bread. We got stuck a few times and it was bitter cold, but it was such an adventure! We also spent time in the winter building igloos and even ice skating on our lawn! You have to make the most out of every situation.
Q. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard everyday?

I would not be where I am today without the incredible support system God has blessed me with. My family, friends, and mentors have pushed me to strive for success, to have a heart for others, and to genuinely care about my impact on the world. I work hard every day to give back to the people who have shaped me and given me the best possible life. I have always believed in the importance of living life to the fullest and embracing every moment. Harvard professor, Tal Ben-Shahar, says, “When you appreciate the good, the good appreciates.” How wonderful is that? Continue working to make each day the best it can be, appreciate how wonderful each day is, and I promise you, your life will be enriched in ways you never thought possible. I continue to be myself because there is no other person that will ever be me, so why would I try to be someone else? We are all made to be unique individuals, and I believe in the beauty of that and how our Earth can prosper from our differences.As I have grown older, I recognize the importance of knowing who I am and my worth, and I would not trade anything to be someone else because it is special to be you. I own up to having flaws and making mistakes, but those things all help us to grow, learn, and prosper.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Peanut butter is absolutely, without a doubt, my guilty pleasure. I love anything and everything peanut butter.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

Obviously becoming Miss Earth is one BIG thing I want to achieve, but the one thing I want to ultimately achieve is that my life positively influenced the people of this world. Crowns and trophies are wonderful, but it is what you do with those achievements that really matter. I want to leave a legacy of positive change in the way we treat ourselves, each other, the earth, and in the way, we respond to issues. I want to help people see the importance of their own lives and the impact they can make on others and our world. So, my ultimate goal is not to win anything, but to be and make a difference.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
Clean water and food for all, enough money to take care of my bills and the bills of my loved ones, and the gift of teleportation to travel anywhere at any time!
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

Thank you for the constant support and love, it means more to me than I could ever begin to express. You are all so much of the reason I continue to push on towards the title of Miss Earth. I am inspired by all of you who continue to spend your time reaching out and helping in any way possible to keep Earth beautiful. I am thoroughly impressed by the dedication of each individual I have met along my journey to plant trees, recycle, and clean up all over the world. Remember, your help does make a difference because even a small pebble can create a ripple, and with more and more ripples we can create waves of change! Sending so much love and appreciation to all of you, and thank you to Angelopedia for interviewing me and allowing me to show y’all my heart.

paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss New England Earth United States 2018 Isabella Brie Bennett sharing her experience and journey of being the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
1. How does it feel to be the winner of Miss New England Earth United States 2018 and a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

Being chosen to hold a title within such a prestigious organization is a blessing, and to be honest it still feels like a dream in the best possible way. I have so much love for where I come from, so having the opportunity to represent my region on a national level is both a privilege and an honor. Every day I get to wake up with the knowledge that I can use my current position to make a positive difference in my community, which is truly something special. If I had to choose one word to describe how it feels to be Miss New England Earth United States 2018 it would be elation.
2. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

There is a quote by the famous Japanese writer RyunosukeSatoro that I feel best communicates the biggest lesson I have learned so far on this odyssey; “Individually, we are one drop. Together, we are an ocean.”. What I love most about the Miss Earth organization is that every delegate on a local, state, and national level has a unified mission of environmental responsibility. When educated and passionate individuals unite for a common cause, our collective voices become a powerful catalyst for change.
3. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

The relationships that I have cultivated over my lifetime are my biggest motivation. My family and friends are everything to me. I am very fortunate to have a wonderful support system behind me and I want to do everything that I can to make them proud. When people willingly choose to stay in your life it means that they see something in you that you might not necessarily see in yourself; that notion absolutely inspires me to try to be the best person that I can possibly be.
4. We would love to know more about your advocacy to save the Planet Earth and what drove you to choose it?

At an early age my parents instilled within me a love and respect for nature. I was brought up to believe that the earth is our home and that it is our responsibility to protect it. As I got older, I began to see the destruction that humanity was inflicting on our planet. It became my personal objective to become better educated about the environment and its deteriorating health. Once I had a better understanding of the challenges and threats that our environment is facing, it was clear to me that man is the biggest problem our planet is facing and that we are also the solution. I knew that I wanted to be at the forefront of the environmentally conscious movement and that the best way for me to do so was to lead by example. I began incorporating sustainable practices into my lifestyle and advocating for our planet by helping others to develop an understanding of what is happening and why these issues matter. By educating others on the impact that humans have on earth’s delicate ecosystems and the organism that call our planet home, my hope is that I can help to create a greener future for the generations that follow.
5. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage of Miss Earth United States 2018?

When competing in a pageant you always want to highlight the best aspects of yourself. I want to be able to emphasize that I am a well-informed, well spoken, confident woman. I walk through life with a sense of purpose and that is something I strive to carry over into my performance. My hope is that I am able to communicate the different facets of my personality through my wardrobe selection and composure on stage.
6. Who is your ideal, if any and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I do not have a singular ideal but rather several individual who possess qualities that I admire. I hold Malala Yousafzai in high esteem for her courage. I admire President Barack Obama’s poise in difficult situations, Ellen DeGeneres’s wit, and Vice President Al Gore’s dedication to the climate crisis. Every person that we encounter has at least one positive attribute that we could benefit from incorporating into our own life. At the end of the day I think the trait that I reverence the most is humility because without it we could not possible see the good in others.
7. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

As a huge comic book fan, I would want to complete some big heroic action like stopping a robbery. Invisibility, even if only for 24 hours, is a super power and it would be cool to do something good for society. However if crime fighting wasn’t an option for the day, I would want to travel somewhere exotic. Just think of how exciting it would be to take a fee solo trip to someplace new. It would be the adventure of a lifetime.
8. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

Everyone has a specific childhood memory that has helped to define who they are as a person and I am very fortunate that mine is a positive memory. For me the most special memory I have is of the day my little brother, William, was born. Holding him for the first time was a defining moment in my life because within an instant I learned that it was possible to give someone your whole heart and expect nothing in return. At eight years old I knew I had a friend for life.
9. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

Finding ways to empower myself is something that I work on continuously. While there is nothing wrong with feeling empowered because of others actions or encouragement, I think being able to self-reflect and find our own inner strength is crucial to our personal development. Our most important relationship is with ourselves and it takes time to learn how to build ourselves up from the inside out. Self-empowerment is a process but a necessary one.
10. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

I love the US television show “Survivor”. I could binge watch an entire season if I had nothing else to do. No-one wants to admit that they love reality TV but it is without a doubt my guilty pleasure.
11. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

My ultimate goal is to create a life that I don’t need a vacation from. I want to be able to make a successful living doing what I love. I want to surround myself with people who nourish my soul. And someday in my old age, I would like to look back at my life and feel as though my existence was both happy and fulfilling.
12. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

If granted three wishes with no limitations, I would first wish to destigmatize mental illness in conjunction with more affordable access to treatment options. I would then wish for the eradication of rape culture from our society. Finally, I would wish for the earth to be able to heal itself faster than the rate at which our species is damaging it.
13. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

I would like to express my love and appreciation to everyone who took the time to read tis interview. Thank you for following my journey to the 2018 Miss Earth United States Pageant and for supporting our organization! To stay up to date on my adventures be sure to follow me on Instagram @isabella.brie and like the official Miss New England Erath United States Facebook page.

dek: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Illinois Earth United States 2018 Kristy Decheva
paragraphs: Miss Earth United States 2018 is all set to organize its grand finale on 14th July 2018 where delegates from all over the States will compete for the national crown. Andreia Gibau, the reigning Miss Earth United States, will crown her successor at the end of the event finale.

But before that, here we have Miss Illinois Earth United States 2018 Kristy Decheva sharing her experience and journey of being the national delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018 in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q. How does it feel to be the winner and delegate for Miss Illinois Earth US 2018?

I feel extremely privileged to represent this great state of Illinois. Thus far, I have been involved in multiple projects that represent and support my platform of Water Conservation. After each appearance and volunteer work I do, I can confidently say that I feel unjustifiably dignified as a delegate to represent Illinois.
Q. What is the best lesson you have learned in your journey as a delegate of Miss Earth United States 2018?

The best lesson I have learned thus far is that beauty queens cannot make everybody happy. In other words, no matter how much one tries to do the right thing, there will always be opposing opinions, the most important thing is to keep your ground and do what is best for you and the people around you.
Q . What is the thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?
My family, each time I have some success in whatever I do, I see how happy it makes my family. That inspires me to be the best version of myself, so I can keep making them proud, every time.
Q . What is your advocacy and why did you choose this?

My platform is ‘Water Conservation’. I chose this to advocate for primarily because of my background. I was raised in an underdeveloped country in the Balkan region of Eastern Europe and we had run into a lot of water shortage issues. Once I immigrated to the US, I was shocked to see how a lot of the people took water for granted, often leaving the sink running when brushing teeth, or taking an hour long showers. We are so grateful to have an abundance of water available here, but we must take into consideration that there are countries out there with no access to clean water. This struck me to start my campaign and teach American youth how we can use up less water in our daily lives.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage?

I would like to represent myself as a legacy for the organization. My goal, whether win or lose, is to begin educational programs in public schools for children. The program will focus on preserving the Earth’s natural resources.
Q. Who is your idol, if any, and what values of their you wish you could include in your own life?

My idol is my mother. If I could have one of her traits to include as my own it would be her bravery. She is not afraid of anything and she has great problem solving skills. Every time I encounter an issue that seems to have no way out, I go to her for advice, because I know that she will point me in the right direction.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you spend it?

If I were invisible for a day, I would spend it to listen to conversations that I wouldn’t have access to with visibility. Why? Well, it’s important to be able to hear people out when you are not there and hear discussing you in front of others, that way you can truly know who is a loyal friend and who is unloyal.
Q. Is there a special childhood memory you’d like to share with us?

My most special childhood memory is Easter day. I remember being so anxious to wake up in the morning and dye eggs with my grandmother. I spent the entire day dying eggs and decorating them, that was one of the most precious memories to me.
Q. Who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

To be honest, that would just be me. There is no one in my mind that I think of daily that really gets my tires spinning. When I wake up, I drink coffee, shower, get dressed, and I am ready to get my day started! Every day is a ‘work hard play harder’ for me!
Q. What is one thing you can label yourself as guilty pleasure?

My guilty pleasure is by far indulging in delicious meals. I have a strict diet but often times I let myself slip because it is just so hard to control cravings for certain meals. For an example, I crave cookies (yummmm) almost every day, but limit myself to having 2 or 3 a week!
Q. What is one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?
I am working very hard right now to practice for my LSAT exams. I want to get accepted to and finish law school from a prestigious university. That is my next goal.
Q. If you were granted three wishes right now, what would you ask for?
1.) For everyone in my family to continue having great health
2.) Wish the best possible life for my sister
3.) Bring world peace
Q. What message would you give to your fans from Angelopedia?
My word of advice would be to never doubt yourself. When one has doubt, he/she is limiting him/herself from full potential. Always believe in yourself, and never, ever, give up on your dreams.

Q . What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

My guilty pleasure would be I adore carbohydrates! Anything really... especially : Mashed potatoes , pizza and, macaroni and cheese . I watch my intake of these foods and lead a very healthy lifestyle including daily working out and eating nutritiously but, I love my carbs!
Q .We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

While I know that there will only be one winner at the end of the Miss Earth United States 2018 pageant and while I hope to be the one chosen to represent the United States, I still want to feel regardless of the outcome, that I represented my beautiful state of Florida well. There are so many other wonderful benefits from participating in a national pageant like this and that even with all the fun, hard work and new friends made at the end of the day... I will still have a crown and sash and can and will still help anyone in need. This is a commitment I have made to myself and state.
Q . If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
If given three wishes I Would ask for healing powers, Super strength, and more wishes ! Lol
Q . Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

My message would be to follow my Facebook and Instagram social media pages! I will be doing a takeover May 23rd at 9 PM EST on Facebook live and also to check out my event that I’m hosting on June 10th . This event is a beach workout/cleanup.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 Finalist Safina Barsatie
dek: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 Finalist Safina Barsatie
paragraphs: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.

The 11 finalists are enjoying every bit of the pageant and are working hard to get closer to the crown. The reigning queen Miss Grand Netherlands 2017, Kelly Van Den Dungen is also spending time with the delegates, giving them tips and sharing her own experience with the girls. The candidates of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 also had a chance to enjoy an official photo shoot with the reigning queen.
But, it’s time we get to know each and every one of them personally. So here is Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 finalist Safina Barsatie’s future plans, and past struggles.
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

Being one of the contestants of Miss Grand Netherlands makes me feel really honored and glad. My participation with this pageant is one of the items of my bucket list. It’s a chance to fulfill one of my dreams so I am really grateful to have this opportunity.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?

The best lesson I’ve have learnt and that has shaped my life is not to take anything for granted. We often don’t appreciate what we have until it’s gone: that includes your health, your family and friends and your job. Nothing in your life is guaranteed to be there tomorrow, including those you love. Be conscious of the value of every single day and make every day count. This is a hard life lesson to learn, but for me it’s the most important of all: Life can change in an instant. Make sure you appreciate what you have, while you still have it.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

The one thing that keeps me going and inspires me to be the best version of myself is to stay positive and have faith. We can only have faith in the future if we have faith in ourselves. If you have faith in your abilities, with a humble but reasonable confidence in your powers you can be happy and successful.
Q. Other than the Miss Grand Netherlands crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?

The most important thing I want to achieve from this competition is to win the people’s hearts. Their support is important for me to achieve my goals. Besides that, I want to gain experience and have a wonderful time with my pageant sisters. But what I mostly look forward is to go international and proudly represent my country.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

One thing that I consider as my life goal is to pursue your dreams, whatever they may be. You only life once. We keeping waiting for that amazing thing to happen in the future that will be the key to our happiness. But this is it. Right now. So follow your dreams before it's to late!
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

I would like to represent myself as a confident woman who works hard to succeed. Someone with a mission and a great personality. A representative woman with a powerful appearance combined with beauty and brains. A great hearted woman who can be a good example for others.
Q. Who is your idol, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

My mom has always been my role model. As a single woman, she showed me how strong a woman can be and has taught me to be an independent woman. She has made me who I am today: “An independent woman who works hard to achieve her goals". Just like her I want to inspire young people by showing them that it doesn’t matter where you come from and what you have been through. Everything is possible if you believe in yourself!
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I would sneak into a chocolate factory for a day, and swipe tastes of EVERYTHING! Or maybe get into a bank vault, take lots of money, and scatter it around some poor areas to make a whole bunch of people’s days.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

I cannot mention a very special moment in my childhood years, because every moment in my life is something that I treasure. Childhood days are a moment where in we are so much secured by our parents. The moment where in the attention is all yours and gave whatever you wished for.
Q. What is your advocacy, can you tell us more about it?

My advocacy is to speak and stand up for people that might not be heard. Especially for those who are victim of war. We often don't realize what impact it has on their lives. They have lost their family, friends, everything that they have built up and love. If I have the chance to help them I would support them at any possible way.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
One thing that I can label as my guilty pleasure is to eat fast food after I went to the gym. I’m always hungry after training so on that moment I love to have a fast and tasty meal.
Q.If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

I would wish everyone to have perfect health at all times, excluding the natural aging process. My second wish would be for everyone to have free education because wisdom is power. And my last wish would be to fill our hearts and mind only with love so there would be no hate and violence anymore.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?
Hi fans! Thank you for reading our interviews. I hope you got to know us better. Keep following us and take care of yourselves!

dek: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.

paragraphs: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.

Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

I feel utterly proud of myself to be one of the beautiful 11 finalists that have been chosen for Miss Grand Netherlands2018, and possibly the one lucky enough to represent our beautiful country on the international stage of Miss Grand International 2018.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?
To think and stay positive at all times and circumstances.
Our attitude and thinking towards life will determine life's attitude toward us.
My favorite quote is: A negative mind will never give you a positive life
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?
“Be the change that you wish to see in the world” this quote inspires me to be the best version of myself.
Because the world won’t change, if you don’t change, we always have to start with looking at ourselves.
Q. Other than the Miss Grand Netherlands crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?
What I would like to achieve from this competition is knowledge and inspiration on how to stop the pain in this world.
Next to making friends with the other awesome delegates, it is nice to see their ideas and knowledge about our world problems.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?
My life goal is to be happy and positive, when I achieve this I can fulfill any dream I have, of which one of them is to travel the world and get to know other cultures.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

I would represent myself just the way that I am, I have come this far into getting in the competition just by being myself; if I would get the honor to win the title of Miss Grand Netherlands it would be because I kept real to myself.
Q. Who is your ideal, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?
I feel really connected to the values of Morgan Freeman, these are some of his values which I totally agree with and are exactly like I would want to think in my life.
“We humans are more concerned with having than with being.
Owning things never brings happiness. Find joy in being. Look around and appreciate the little things – the morning sky, wind blowing on your face, the sound of birds chirping.”
“How do we change the world? One random act of kindness at a time.
Small goals hold much more power than you think they do. If you want to change the world, do a small gesture today. Real power lies in the present.”
“challenge yourself it's the only path which leads to growth”
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I would go to Amsterdam Airport and step into a plane that travels to one of the countries I’d like to visit (which are a lot, so I would probably go for a warm climate since it is mostly 9/12 months cold in The Netherlands)
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?
My most special childhood memory would the day I got my first puppy.
I was asking my parents every day to get a puppy and (eventually) they gave in, we called him Bruno and I have had him for 10 years, unfortunally he died of cancer when I was 18.
Q. What is your advocacy, can you tell us more about it?
My advocacy is to spread awareness on violence against women all around the world, who are victims of war.
Violence against women, especially rape, has added its own brand of shame to wars.
When in war It has been said that most civilians tend to die from war rather than in battle. And women have ended up on the front-line, not as soldiers but as victims.
Victims of people who think they have the right to put their hands on someone else’s body.
People who have been guilty of rape in war and yet do not get prosecuted for their deeds.

To overcome the physical and psychological trauma of rape and other forms of sexual violence should not be underestimated, women can and mostly will suffer from depression, anxiety disorders, flashbacks, difficulties in re-establishing intimate relationships, and fear.
I want to be the voice to support these women and stand up against violence against women in war.

At this moment I am collaborating with the charity of “Doctors without borders”, I have started a crowd funding action on Facebook where people can donate a small amount of money to support this charity.
Doctors Without Border helps people worldwide where the need is the greatest, delivering emergency medical aid to people affected by conflict, epidemics, disasters, or exclusion from health care.
To change “what is” into “what should be”.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
FOOD!!! Noodles, pizza, sushi…. I can continue for a while
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
My first wish would be: No more suffering in this world for all living being. No war, no hunger, no pain, but instead equality and understanding.
My second wish is: Since I was a little kid I have always dreamed of talking to animals, so this would be my second wish.
My third wish would be and yes I am serious about this one haha: To make the whole Harry Potter world real, a real Hogwarts for wizards and witches and the ability to practice magic.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?
I feel so beloved because of the support that I get from the people that support me in the pageant of becoming Miss Grand Netherlands 2018.

I hope I will make the people who are rooting for me proud if I would be the one to get the honor to win the title, and if this would happen I hope my fans would support me to the international stage of Miss Grand International as it would be the most amazing experience of my life.

I grew up in a loving environment. In spite of the divorce of my parents when I was 4 years old, I received as much love from my father as my mother. My parents have always been good friends with each other so far. My parents are 100% behind me in all positive that I want to achieve in my life.
Q. What is your advocacy; can you tell us more about it?
My advocacy is Stop War and Violence. I will inspire all the people in need and authorities to take concrete steps to stop the war and start war preventing activities.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

I love watching TV series like “The Flash, it’s about helping people, The Walking Dead about how to survive and Empire about family love” These series are very interesting and I can watch them every day. As soon as one of these series touch me, I get tears in my eyes. Especially when the storyline on those series are based on a true story.
Q. If you are granted three wishes right now, what would you ask for?

If I had three wishes. I would wish for love, peace and happiness because we all need to feel and be loved. This let us become better people. Peace is important in life. There are too many wars countries. Nationalities and religion always struggling against instead of coming together as one people on this earth. If everyone is happy, this world would be better and people would always look out for each other.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?

We are all humans and we all make mistakes. The most important thing is to understand that there are different people with different opinions and different points of view. But that makes every single person unique. Give love to everyone, than we can work together, Let we use our potential to those who need it.

paragraphs: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.

The candidates of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 also had a chance to enjoy an official photo shoot with the reigning queen.
But, it’s time we get to know each and every one of them personally. So here is Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 finalist Lisan Weidgraaf’s future plans, and past struggles.
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

To be a delegate of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 feels amazing. It feels like a dream coming true and to be honest, I don’t want this dream to end. Miss Grand Netherlands is already such a beautiful experience. All the girls are so sweet and we have the best organization. And I am really proud to be part of something bigger.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?

The best lesson that I have learnt in live is to be always true to who you are. When you change who you are for someone else, you will never find happiness. And that is why I will always do my best to be myself in the best way possible.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

When I see people I love reach their goals and dreams gives me so much happiness. It makes me believe in myself even more because of their successes. It gives me strength to reach my goals and inspiration to just keep going. It shows me that as long as you believe in yourself, the sky is really the limit.
Q. Other than the Miss Grand Netherlands crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?

I know for a fact that the Miss Grand Netherlands pageant will give me so much. It already gave me the best pageant-sisters. But it will also give me so much personal growth in the greatest way possible.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

The main goal I have in life is that my family, my friends and I are healthy and happy. That we can enjoy every part of all wonderful things in life. I hope that I can make the world better for everyone, even when it is just a little bit.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

I would like to represent myself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 as the real me. I am a happy woman who loves to achieve her goals and dreams, which is eager to learn and wants to show everyone to always be the best version of yourself. And I hope I can show this on the finale.
Q. Who is your ideal, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

My ideal is my mother. I have so much respect for how strong and independent she is. When there is a setback she turns the situation around and makes the best out of it, in a way that life is even better after. This positive look on life is so inspirational, I try to live by this and share this with others.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I love this question, but it is also a really hard one. If I could be invisible for a day I would love to swim in the sea next to all the sea life or go in to nature and watch all the animals. Normally they would swim or run away from people but because I am invisible they will just act how they always do. I think it is very interesting to see them in their natural habitat.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My most special childhood memory is a very specific one. When I was in elementary school I always biked by my grandparents’ house. They always put a little candy in their mailbox for me to find and they were standing in front of the window to wave at me when I passed by on my bike. I loved it so much to be able to see them every single day, it showed me that they loved me and it is still the best memory I have.
Q. What is your advocacy; can you tell us more about it?

My advocacy is to help other people in every way you can. If you feel like that you need to help refugees, do it. If you can only miss a little bit of money, donate it. If you see someone on the street that needs help, help them. If you give and help people wherever you can, you will make live a little bit better by every action.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
My guilty pleasure is that I sometimes can get so much joy out of doing absolutely nothing, just sitting on the couch with my animals and with a candy bar. Relaxing and thinking about life.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

If I have 3 wishes, my first wish would be to be able to travel everywhere in the world in just one minute time forever, to zap myself everywhere in the world. This would give me the chance to see everything in the world. My second wish is to be able to speak every language in the world, so I can communicate with everyone where I have zapped myself. And of course, my third wish would be that there is no more war and violence in the world. That everyone can enjoy their lives and be happy.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?

The message that I would like to give to everyone is to just be yourself, in the best way possible. If you believe in yourself and go for it. Be positive and never let anybody else tell you that you are not good enough or that something is not possible.

Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

Since I was a child, I always watched the Miss Universe Final on the television. For me it was just a dream and I kept telling myself that it was only a real thing for some lucky girls in the world. At that time competing in a pageant looked so far away. Not only because of my age back then, but also because of the thought that I would never be good enough to be like those pretty girls on TV.

In 2016, I came in touch for the first time with the pageant world, namely Miss Beauty of the Netherlands. I was selected as provincial finalist and was so happy at that time, not knowing that I would win the provincial title and as well the big final at the end. I became Miss Beauty of the Netherlands 2016! I learned a lot during that journey and came to the conclusion that I was not done with participating in 0+pageants.

I decided to register myself for Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 and I can proudly say that I am one of the finalists for the big title. I feel so blessed and proud, because the pageant stands for something meaningful. I love being an ambassador for ‘stop the war and violence’ that the pageant stands for.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?

I live by the quote: If something becomes hard, work harder. If you have a dream, go for it. Never let people drop you down. In the past people told me that I was not good enough, not smart enough and that I was too ambitious. In the beginning I felt so bad when somebody told me that I was not good or strong enough to accomplish something. Instead of good energy it gave me bad energy which you cannot use when you have a goal in mind. At that time I started to realize that how much energy you need to invest in something, that if you like it, it will automatically give you energy back. And that is the right spirit. Besides that always be yourself, we only live once. Let’s live life to the fullest.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

I think that every person has a light in their heart that is lighting up on moments you really want to reach something. That light is giving you power to conquer the bad moments and as well to focus really on what you want to achieve. I can rely this on multiple examples in my life, my work, my sport but as well during the pageant. I believe that if you really want to reach your goal, you can make it, as long if the mindset is good. Listen good to your heart and everything will be alright.

Sometimes it is okay to talk with the people you love. Share your story and you will see that they’re behind you and that they will support you no matter what. I often say, teamwork makes a dream work and for me it really is.
Q. Other than the Miss Grand Netherlands crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?

I want to become the best version of myself. Every time you are wearing your sash is a moment to remember what you have already accomplished. It gives me self-confidence and it reminds me where I stand for. I really want to be an inspiration for other people. The 17th of June we will know who the new Miss Grand Netherlands is and at that point I want to look in the mirror and say to myself that I learned as much as possible during the journey. For me the inner beauty is really important, so I want to use these months of preparation to focus on this point.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

My life goal is definitely being happy. If I’m happy, I smile and when I smile, I feel strong. Besides that I hope to have a happy family someday and that I have my own company. I always had the feeling that I wanted to do something for the society and I know with my empathy and educational background in Psychology, I can help people. That is for me a life goal that I would like to focus on.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

I’m really looking forward to the finals of Miss Grand Netherlands. For me beauty from the outside is important, but the inner beauty is for sure even important for me. By sporting a lot and eating healthy I try to look as good as possible, but besides that I want to represent myself really as Kimberley. The confident, sweet and hardworking woman with a positive mindset who is able to achieve goals and I hope the judges will see this during the finals.
Q. Who is your ideal, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

My parents are my ideal. They raised me and my little sister with lots of love and they always supported us in the choices we made. They told me that it is important to find the real you, so they always gave me the space to discover how I wanted to live my life.
This is something that I really admire and it’s is also something that I encourage to other children.

Reading this questions reminds me as well about my work. I’m currently working in a consultancy company focusing on engineering. I speak with people from all around the world and for me it’s really important that they are doing something that they like. When I talk to people I always try to find out what makes them happy and that they are going to do something that they love to do. This is in line with what my parents learned me as a child.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

Well, that is an easy question for me. If I could be invisible for one day, I would secretly take the first plane as possible to Canada where a part of my family is living. Family means a lot to me and it would be wonderful to see them again after a long time. Even though they can’t see me, I still would appreciate it to see them again.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

The most special childhood memory for me was the trip to Canada. I went with my family to Canada to visit our family there and that was so special for me. We traveled around the country, visited culture and nature. I remember the trips in the car for hours and that we were talking about everything that came up into our minds. At that moment I forgot the beautiful nature around me, because I was so happy to be with my family and that gives me such a nice feeling when I think about that trip.
Q. What is your advocacy; can you tell us more about it?

I want to raise awareness for people and especially children in times of war. At this moment it is a urgent global problem that we need to solve together. We need to be strong and need to take action on it. Not only looking at it. Mom’s and dad’s are losing their children, children are losing their friends and so on and it’s all because of war and violence. We can’t let this happen….

In the Netherlands, we welcomed lots of refugees last year and that means a lot to me. It shows the good side of the people in our country. Now I have a clear vision that I want to accomplish. I want to visit some refugee places and spend some time with them. I would like to understand their story and take away the pain a bit for a while. With my background in psychology I learned how to communicate with people, but also in some cases, how to find back a smile on somebody’s face and that would mean the world to me. I am aware that I cannot change the world by myself, but if everybody starts looking at themselves, than we can make a difference together.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
SUSHI! You literally can wake me up for this in the middle of the night. Especially the ones with salmon on it, I love it!
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
Well, to be Miss Grand Netherlands of course and having the honor to represent the Netherlands in Miss Grand International 2018.
Secondly I want to wish for health and happiness for the people who are standing close to me.
At last giving me and other people the power and the tools to help the people who are in need, because together we can make a difference.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?

First of all thank you for having this interview with me and besides that, thank you so much for supporting us all in our journey to the crown of Miss Grand Netherlands. I promise to do the best I can do during the competition! <3

paragraphs: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.

The 11 finalists are enjoying every bit of the pageant and are working hard to get closer to the crown. The reigning queen Miss Grand Netherlands 2017, Kelly Van Den Dungen is also spending time with the delegates, giving them tips and sharing her own experience with the girls. The candidates of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 also had a chance to enjoy an official photo shoot with the reigning queen.
But, it’s time we get to know each and every one of them personally. So here is Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 finalist Jeanne Molenaar’s future plans, and past struggles.
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

At the moment I’m living a very fulfilling life. Although I’ve never participated in a beauty contest before I feel right at home during the preparations. I’ve met a lot of kind contestants. Meeting new people, searching for new trends in make-up and fashion is something I adore.

My daily life is centered on my life’s work as a nurse. Since I think it is important to build relationships on trust I provide my patients with all the love and care, even when that is sometimes difficult. A lifelong dream can now be fulfilled: becoming a model! The road to this goal is paved with charity too. Being a model, being pretty is not the only goal.
During the competition and promotion I strive to give the people around me a deeper message. The two things I like the most. Howe awesome can it be!?
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?

When I was younger, I used to get bullied. This made me very insecure, and I didn’t love myself anymore. It took many years to get my confidence back. Over the years I learned to trust people more and knowing that there are still nice and generous people.
Because of this I’ve learned to love and enjoy my life and to be kind to others.
Something as simple as a smile can brighten someone's day!
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?
In my profession you see a lot of people who are ill and pass away. Some people inspire you; they endure so much and still remain positive and kind to others. Honestly, I think it’s admirable.
For me, there are kind people around me who support me and bring out the best in me there is so much misery in this world, which makes me realize to cherish what we have.
Q. Other than the Miss Grand Netherlands crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?
I want to become proud of myself and I want to do good for others. Raise awareness for people who need it.
To be a famous model is also something I want to achieve.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?
To spread some care, attention and love to the people around me and my (future) family.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?
As a sweet and elegant village girl who lives by high normal standards.
Q. Who is your idol, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

Beyoncé is my idol, because she breathes respect to all. Whether you’re Caucasian, Afro-American, gay or straight, all people are treated with respect. And she shows this in her lyrics of her songs. She makes a statement about discrimination and she is a real power woman. People who listen to her songs get strength from the lyrics. She is writing history because she is at this moment the most famous female artist who stands up for black people and she lets hear her opinion about discrimination.
The values of her need to be brought to the next generation so there will be less hatred in the world, and more love for each other. And that’s what I am going to do!
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
I would like to follow Beyoncé for one day. To see if she’s really happy and what her daily life looks like.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

There are so many special memories in my childhood. Because I am raised in a loving family. But the most special moment for me, was when I went to a different school, after I was being bullied. In the different school they welcomed me with open arms. That change, that feeling of love from people I had never met before made me realize that for every low there’s a new high. This knowledge made me to the strong person I am today.
Q. What is your advocacy; can you tell us more about it?

May, fourth, and fifth are Dutch Memorial days. During those days thoughts and prayers are sent to the victims of the Second World War. During the fourth we think of the victims and during the fifth we celebrate the liberation of Holland.
The theme van Miss Grand is: ’Stop the war and violence’.

Luckily, Holland knows no war at this moment. Something we should be very thankful of. Because of this gratitude and my strong opinion that freedom is ever so important, I wanted to spread the message of the importance of freedom. While we, Dutch people live in freedom and think this is absolutely our right and virtue, other people suffer day by day. There goes the normality of our situation.

During May, fourth and fifth our creed will be ‘Pass on the freedom’ so this is the time when I want to create awareness amongst our people! How will I do that? By handing out small pins with the national emblem of May, Fourth and Fifth. People can wear these pins of give them to other people and show gratitude for our way of life. Furthermore I want to know what the Dutch people think about all this and how they experience their freedom.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Don’t tell anyone, but, secretly, I sing and dance to guilty pleasure music. You can always wake me for a good old Disney-classic. Yes, even at midnight.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

Sorry to go with the clichés, but I wish for a warless world full of health and prosperity. On a side-note I could just ask the genie in the bottle for the largest walk-in closet of the world. Filled of course with the finest dresses and all! Girls will be girls…
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?

Go with the clichés. Stay calm and be yourself, everybody else is taken! See the good and the worth in everybody and everything. Feel the appreciation for each new day that you can spend in freedom, in health and with love. Mythical cliché, but still my truth to you all.
Be yourself and be happy about it.

Currently I am supporting the Netherlands Refugee Foundation. The work that they do is so brave!
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

I consider graduating from my Master’s Degree at the age of 20 as a real milestone. This was during the time that my father became very ill and passed away. The fact that I was still able to keep working hard made myself, my family and him very proud (I’m sure of it!)
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

As a shining light! I am excited to convey my heart and character in the form of a speech and hope to inspire everyone around me about what it means to be a person that looks to serve others instead of living a life solely for myself.
Q. Who is your idol, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

My parents, definitely. Both of them are great leaders and teachers, and I am very grateful for the life lessons that they have taught me. They showed me how meaningful it is to invest in others, to run the extra mile and put your own interests on the background sometimes. I really honor them for that!
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I would love to see the inside of the White House and shortly observe how political meetings are being held. I’m very curious you know. It’s also a great possibility to travel to beautiful places, such as the 7 Wonders of the World, I wouldn’t have to get in line for anything!
Also, I would obviously pull a few pranks on my friends. Can’t leave that one out.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My most special childhood memory is the exact moment I met my best friend, which is now 11 years ago. It was a short conversation of just two sentences, but from that point on we have build up a great, life lasting friendship. I know my life would be very different if we had not met each other when we were younger. And ever since we made so many memories together, so I wouldn’t be able to just pick one.
Q. What is your advocacy, can you tell us more about it?

I am all about research and education. I love to write, teach and speak at events. We can easily assume the things that we hear around us for reality and truth, which then shapes the collective psychology. I always advocate to be critical and to make sure to ask questions first. Out of many things that we should and could be, make sure that being an objective researcher is one of your priorities. Our mental frame affects our behavior, which plays a crucial role in either preventing or stimulating different issues, such as wars or discrimination.

I love that the Netherlands Refugee Foundation also provides education to children who can’t go to school because of dangerous circumstances. I can’t stretch enough how important this is in my opinion.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

I love Japanse anime and Korean dramas and every time I’ll tell myself that I’m gonna sleep early this night, I turn on another episode. Those cliffhangers! But... I’m still always in time for work the next day, hehe.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
A world filled with a vision of unity, humility and collective moral values, despite our differences. I don’t think that wish is too big :)
I also love, love, LOVE avocado’s, so a tree that’s always full of it and free to pick from is my ultimate dream.
The ability to fly. Really, how awesome is that?! I know I’m not the only one who wishes for it!
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?
Thank you for simply following Miss Grand Netherlands! I wouldn’t have the opportunity to be so open about all this if it wasn’t for you guys!

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 Finalist Esmeralda Carelse
dek: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 Finalist Esmeralda Carelse
paragraphs: Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 took a rocking start with twelve finalists. However, due to an unfortunate turn of events, one of the finalists, Deborah Van Hemert, had to back off. Now, only 11 finalists remain as the coronation night nears us.

The 11 finalists are enjoying every bit of the pageant and are working hard to get closer to the crown. The reigning queen Miss Grand Netherlands 2017, Kelly Van Den Dungen is also spending time with the delegates, giving them tips and sharing her own experience with the girls. The candidates of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 also had a chance to enjoy an official photo shoot with the reigning queen.
But, it’s time we get to know each and every one of them personally. So here is Miss Grand Netherlands 2018 finalist Esmeralda Carelse’s future plans, and past struggles.
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

I am completely new to the pageant world. When I was scouted, just before the casting, I couldn't imagine myself develop the way I did since. The jury of the election gave me a great opportunity and has not only given me a great self-confidence boost, but also helped me grow as a young woman. My drive in life has always been to help the people around me. As a little girl I would always give the money I got for my birthday to the people who needed it more than me. I was raised with the important value to always help others, and for this reason I continue to do a lot of volunteer work for different organizations.
Q. What is the best lesson you've learnt that has shaped your life?

Living in a time where we are pressured to live the perfect life, can lead to a lot of insecurities. We are very focused on our online presence and we take everything we see on social media as a reality, which can cause self doubt. This was one of the reasons I had a burn-out in 2015. It was a very challenging time for me. I had to rediscover myself and what I find important as a person. Now, after this period, I am able to look at life in a different light, and I taught myself to be happy with who I am and to not judge others: knowing that everyone goes through their own difficulties.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

I find my peace in writing down my thoughts and feelings. I have a diary which I would recommend to everyone. The trick I use is to write to myself as if I am writing to one of my closest friends. Doing this gives me a lot of new insights about life but mostly myself. Sometimes I go back in time in my diary to see how I developed as a person. This gives me motivation to always continue to write.
Q. Other than the Miss Grand Netherlands crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?

Being scouted gave me this amazing opportunity to take myself seriously. I saw myself grow in such a short time and it is absolutely amazing. I feel blessed to be able to experience this. Since the competition, my self-confidence has grown and I became more comfortable in connecting with the people around me. With the feedback I challenge myself to step outside my comfort zone and to be more critical. This also helped me grow which has been the best part of the journey so far.
Q. We're sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

Currently I am studying Online Media. I find it very interesting how you can easily reach the world through the internet. What I want to achieve is creating an online platform aimed at all young women worldwide. In many countries women cannot go to school due to certain social issues. I find this very sad. Everyone should have the chance to get a proper education to gain knowledge of the world. With my online platform, I want to teach young women how to be independent by teaching them different things and giving them tools for building and developing their own start-up. In addition I want to be able to offer space for self-development and I want to make sexual education a topic for discussion. If I can inspire women to be independent and happy, then I have achieved my life goal.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Grand Netherlands 2018?

My personal goal is not to show how I want to represent myself, but who I have become. The jury saw me for the first time a few weeks ago and I would love for them to see my growth within this short time. I showed up at the casting with no make-up, had no clue what to expect, borrowed my roommate’s bikini, got uncomfortably nervous because everyone was so beautiful and elegant. I always feel comfortable being a laid-back girl with no make-up, wearing t-shirt, jeans and sneakers. But now that I am in this election I am pushed to explore my feminine side and to embrace it. To be honest, I love it and I feel empowered by it. I hope that I can inspire others as well to challenge themselves and to love themselves because we only have one life to be the best versions of ourselves.
Q. Who is your idol, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

There is not a specific person who inspires me. It is the combination of statements, thoughts and performances of different people who can inspire me. Whether you are a belly dancer or a nobel prize winning scientist, what is important is that you are fully enjoying whatever it is that you're doing. But what I find most important in life is to motivate the next generations to love. Love for yourself, love the earth and love others.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
Travel 24/7.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

Growing up in the beautiful city of Amsterdam, there wasn't a lot of nature surrounding me. The closest I got to a chicken was in a supermarket. After school I would always spend my time with friends on the playground and we would all be home for diner by 6 o'clock. A safe and structured life, you can say. Once every two years we went to my family in a small village in Indonesia for two months. This was quiet different from my life in Amsterdam. Indonesia is a beautiful country with breathtaking jungles, rivers and mountains. I would climb trees, hunt in the jungle with my uncles and buy chickens on the market to resell them or slaughter them myself. I had no idea that a pineapple grew out of a plant. I got to know nature there. I was not aware of it at the time, but now that I am older I realize how special it is and how grateful I am to grow up in two completely different worlds.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Pizza! next question.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

To be able to travel all over the world and meet people from different cultures. Respect for one another, whatever the persons religion, race, sexual preference or gender may be. And I would love to have my own farm.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?
It is a cliché, but clichés are there for a reason. Find yourself beautiful and love yourself. Do what makes you happy.
As soon as you believe in yourself, your environment will also believe in you.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Serbia 2018 Ivana Trišić
dek: Talking to Miss Serbia 2018 has turned out a truly delightful event. Ivana Trišic was crowned Miss Serbia 2018 on on 11th October 2017. She will represent Serbia at the Miss World 2018 competition, where Miss World 2017 Manushi Chhillar will be crowning her…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Serbia 2018 Ivana Trišić
paragraphs: Talking to Miss Serbia 2018 has turned out a truly delightful event. Ivana Trišic was crowned Miss Serbia 2018 on on 11th October 2017. She will represent Serbia at the Miss World 2018 competition, where Miss World 2017 Manushi Chhillar will be crowning her successor.

Ivana is 21 years of age and hails from Obrenovac, Belgrade. She bested 20 other candidates to clinch the coveted title of Miss Serbia 2018. She is currently the final year student of law and aspires to become a famous lawyer one day so as to fulfil the promise she has given to her late mother.

She is not just a beautiful face but is also known for her social works. "Do well to others and it will come back to you," is what she believes in. Her role model is Irina Shayk, one of the most beautiful models in the world who also does humanitarian work, and she loves Monica Belucci for her femininity and classical beauty.
So without further ado, let’s get to know Miss Serbia 2018 Ivana Trišic a bit better.
Q. How does it feel to be crowned as Miss Serbia 2018?

Since October last year, when I became Miss Serbia, my life changed completely. First I won the title of Miss Belgrade, which enabled me to directly qualify for the finals. I could not believe when last year's winner Andelija Rogic handed me the crown. I feel very honored and I cannot wait to find out which country will host Miss World.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Serbia 2018?

So far this is an unforgettable experience. I had the opportunity to visit Morocco and France where I spoke to the Serbian ambassador about potential humanitarian activities. I learned that it is most important to be patient and that all our ideas can be achieved if we give our maximum.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

Learning new things has always been a great motivator for me. In every job I've had, I believe I've always been able to learn something new. I am also inspired by people who are struggling for their dreams, who erase prejudices and barriers that society sets us up.
Q. We would love to know more about your advocacy and what drove you to choose it?

My advocacy is to inform women to take care of their health. Every year, a thousand women die from cancer. A lot of them today would be among us if they had regular preventive examinations with a doctor. One of these women is my late mother, who unfortunately recently lost her battle with cancer. I plan to organize several activities to inform women about cancer. I want them to know how healthy nutrition and exercise is important to our health
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Serbia 2018?
I want to introduce myself as a young, socially engaged woman who is ready to change the world for the better.
Q. We have got to know that you recently lost your mother. Our sincere condolences. But what values of hers do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

Thank you for sincere condolence. My mother was my best friend. She always told me: If you do a good job for others, you heal yourself at the same time, because a dose of joy is a spiritual cure. It transcends all barriers.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

Being invisible for a day will give me the opportunity to experience life in a completely new way. I would like to visit the world's greatest wonders, such as the pyramids, and to explore their hidden spaces.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?
My most beautiful memories are related to family trips at sea. Remembering these memories brings me back to life when I was the happiest.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
A large number of people agree on one thing – the treasury of the smells and tastes of traditional Serbian cuisine is very hard to resist. Chocolate soufflé is my biggest weakness.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?
Miss World title is definitely my big dream. I would also like to graduate next year at the Law School and become a lawyer who will fight for the rights of women and children internationally.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
If I could choose three wishes, the first one would be to revive my mother, the second is the health for my family, the third to become a Miss World and to empower every woman.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

I want to thank all the fans for the great support they provide to all the girls that are competing. I am happy with the beautiful message that I receive from you and I will try to fulfill your expectations. Greetings from Serbia.
