title: Beauty Talks with Miss Earth New Zealand 2018 finalist Rove Milford
dek: Miss Earth New Zealand is slowly bringing out all its contestants for the world to see. These girls are here to make a change, and each and every one of them is in full preparation mode for their competition.
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Earth New Zealand 2018 finalist Rove Milford
paragraphs: Miss Earth New Zealand is slowly bringing out all its contestants for the world to see. These girls are here to make a change, and each and every one of them is in full preparation mode for their competition.

It’s necessary that you find out more about these girls before you which one you want to support. So here we reveal the personality of the beautiful Rove Milford in an exclusive interview, talking about her dreams, and advocacies.
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Earth New Zealand 2018?

Being a delegate of Miss Earth New Zealand has been amazing and I have enjoyed every single moment of this journey. It has been wonderful to be a part of a competition with a great batch of women who are willing to exchange knowledge with one another and collectively use our voice to promote environmental sustainability.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?

I have learnt that it is okay to take sacrifices in order to fulfil your dreams. These sacrifice may negatively affect your life in the short term. But, have patience and those sacrifices will eventually pay off.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

My parents have always been my motivators in life. The sacrifices that they have made for their families, has taught me to have perseverance to achieve goals and to stay resilient through tough times. The immense support they have given me throughout my life and this journey has encouraged me to give it my all. Hopefully, one day, I could return the favour back for their support.
Q. Other than the Miss earth New Zealand crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?

I want to savour and enjoy every moment of this competition with fellow contestants and organisers. To gain friendships and moments that I will cherish for the rest of my life. But also, being able to expand my knowledge about the environment and use my position to actively participate in environmental projects that I would hope change people’s perception about the environment.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Earth New Zealand 2018?

It’s wonderful to represent myself on a national stage, it is a good medium for me to confidently express my views about the environment to audience and interact with them. It’s not very often an individual can represent themselves at a national level, so, I will definitely bring out my quirky personality on stage.
Q. Who is your ideal, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I have always admire people who are willing to give up their time to serve their community. Princess Diana has always been a great example of this, she used her platform as a member of the British Royal Family and a public figure to actively advocate issues that were overlooked by society, such as; HIV/AIDS, Leprosy and campaign against landmines, just to name a few. No matter what platform you stand on in life or in your career, It is always important to use your voice, if you want to have change in the community.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
Catch a flight to Queenstown. It is definitely one place in New Zealand I have always wanted to visit.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

Throughout most of my childhood, I was quite a tomboy and I always loved motorsports. Every October, I would wake up early (around 6.30am), grab some snacks, switch on the tv and watch the 6 hour race of the Bathurst 1000 with my father. My father and I would always vocally support Holdens (a car manufacturer) or drivers from New Zealand which annoyed the entire neighbourhood.
Q. What is your advocacy; can you tell us more about it?

My advocacy is Sustainable fishing. Since 80% of our global fish stocks are overfished or exploited, I want to encourage consumers to be more aware of where their seafood and fish products come from. We can all mitigate this problem by simply looking on the can or online on whether particular seafood companies do practice sustainable fishing or have been approved by the Marine Stewardship Council. By doing this, we can influence governments and fish industries to take a more sustainable approach on fishing.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Eat salted dried fish with rice. I could it for the rest of life if I can, but it’s so bad for my cholesterol and blood pressure.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

To finish my degree in Security Studies and being able to work for New Zealand customs or Ministry Foreign Affairs and Trade. I want to make the most of my academic knowledge to protect our border and provide the best interest for all New Zealanders. Through this goal, I would hope to make my parents proud and inspire the younger generations to dream big.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

Firstly, I would like a world where everyone looks beyond people’s physical imperfections and focus on the character of a person. Secondly, where everyone do not use their phones for the day and physically communicate with one another. Lastly, free reusable menstrual products for all women!
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

I would thank everyone who have supported me throughout this journey, I really do appreciate it. Anyone can be an eco-warrior so please be aware of what products you are buying and how you discharge rubbish. Your actions in the present day will impact the lifestyle for future generations to come.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Earth Guyana 2018 finalist Anasa Williams
dek: Miss Earth Guyana 2018 finalist Anasa Williams is all set to compete for the national finale where 8 other contestants will fight for the title. The winner of Miss Earth Guyana 2018 will represent her country at Miss Earth 2018.
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Earth Guyana 2018 finalist Anasa Williams
paragraphs: Miss Earth Guyana 2018 finalist Anasa Williams is all set to compete for the national finale where 8 other contestants will fight for the title. The winner of Miss Earth Guyana 2018 will represent her country at Miss Earth 2018.
In an exclusive interview by Angelopedia, Anasa shares her future plans and aspirations, her experience so far in the competition as well as a few quirky bits.
Below is her full interview –
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Earth Guyana 2018?
It feels incredible to be a delegate of Miss Earth Guyana 2018, I'm genuinely honored.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Earth Guyana 2018?

The best lesson I have learnt in my journey with Miss Earth so far is that I determine the outcome of whatever endeavor i pursue because only I can keep me back as fear and faith have one thing in common they make u believe in something that is yet to occur.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

The one thing that keeps me going and inspires me to be the best version of me is what is at the end of this journey, not just the crown but the level of influence that comes with it. I will finally have a voice loud enough to influence a vast number of people and make a difference.
Q. We would love to know more about your advocacy for Miss Earth 2018 and what drove you to choose it?

My advocacy for Miss Earth Guyana is “New Agricultural Techniques to eradicate G.M.O's". That abbreviation stands for genetically modified organisms which are any living thing that had had their D.N.A or genetic makeup altered through genetic engineering. A lot of fruits and vegetables are currently undergoing this process but use overtime has detrimental effects. Research has shown that cultivation of these foods tend to create super weeds that are resistant to glyph sate a herbicide frequently used in G.M.O foods, they also their own insecticide and humans unwittingly consume this lading to the development of cancerous cells over time. They do not only harm the environment but humans also and I would love to see them totally stamped out because i care about our planet.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Earth Guyana 2018?

I would represent myself as a confident, kind, fierce warrior of the earth, a young woman who has heard Mother Earth's cries and have heeded them, a human who cares about the future of our planet and what future generations will have left for them to enjoy.
Q. Who is your idol and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I would not use idol I would say role model and that person is my grandma. I would like to incorporate her level of patience, confidence and the unlimited amount of determination she has into my life. It's not that I don't have these qualities but I have not reached her level yet.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

If I could be invisible for a day I would spend it rescuing endangered animals and in as much seminars as earth friendly seminars as possible around the world gathering information to make Guyana a green, GMO, litter free country so that others may follow suit.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?
I have so many special ones but the most special one was the first time planted a tree, I got a feeling of joy and now that tree bears a ton of mangoes every season.
Q. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

The drive to go good, the feeling of fulfillment when I would have achieved a goal the overall excitement in seeing the end so near and the fact that someone is always watching and looking up to you as their role model is what empowers me to be myself and work hard every day.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

The one thing I can label as my guilty pleasure is raiding all of my grandma's fruit trees and making a jumbo smoothie with a cheese and tomato sandwich and sit on the roof staring at the trees and the sunset.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?
The one thing I want to ultimately achieve after all of this is over win the crown or not is a group of friends with one common goal save our planet, our home, our earth.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

If I was granted 3 wishes I would ask for an endless supply of wishes, secondly I would wish that the ozone layer would go back to its state before air pollution came into play, thirdly I would wish our oceans were pure again and I will combat the other issues with my endless supply of wishes.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

To my fans here on Angelopedia, life is short but you can make a difference your micro efforts will surely have a magnified effect. So join me in the cause to save our planet, our country, our home. As you do so acknowledge both your fears and your faiths because they both make you believe in something that is yet to happen.

title: Beauty Talks with Miss Earth New Zealand 2018 finalist Jzayla Hughey
dek: Miss Earth New Zealand is slowly bringing out all its contestants for the world to see. These girls are here to make a change, and each and every one of them is in full preparation mode for their competition.
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Miss Earth New Zealand 2018 finalist Jzayla Hughey
paragraphs: Miss Earth New Zealand is slowly bringing out all its contestants for the world to see. These girls are here to make a change, and each and every one of them is in full preparation mode for their competition.

It’s necessary that you find out more about these girls before you which one you want to support. So here we reveal the personality of the beautiful Jzayla Hughey in an exclusive interview, talking about her dreams, and advocacies.
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Earth New Zealand 2018?
Very exciting as this journey has already been so fulfilling. I feel it is a great responsibility to share my new knowledge with those around me and to be the best role model I possibly can be.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt that has shaped your life?
Always challenge yourself and don’t be afraid to step outside your comfort zone! It is important to set goals, chase your dreams and never ever give up.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?
I am fortunate enough to have a positive attitude and strong resilience. My family keeps me going as they are supportive and encouraging in every decision I make.
Q. Other than the Miss earth New Zealand crown, what do you want to achieve from this competition?

Being a part of this pageant has allowed me to build amazing friendships and participate in new experiences and community activities such as eco gardening. By expanding my knowledge in environmental issues I feel I have more confidence in advocating for change.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Earth New Zealand 2018?
It would be wonderful for the general audience to be able to relate to me in a way that encourages them to make simple changes to protect the environment.
Q. Who is your ideal and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

I admire anyone who starts from the bottom and works hard to get their way to the top while remaining genuine and humble. Barrack Obama has always devoted his time to bettering the community even before his reign as President. He began advocating for civil rights as a community organiser, until attending Law school to build his knowledge and ability to do more for the community. As President he continued to advocate for civil rights, healthcare, the environment and many more important causes. Everyone has the potential to do something good for our community.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
Setting all caged and tortured animals free. I was encouraged by my time spent at the Big Cat Rescue in Florida where caged and injured animals were rescued and habilitated.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?
Being part of an ABC kid’s game show with my sister and best friend, which was (embarrassingly) broadcasted every year until I was in high school!
Q. What is your advocacy; can you tell us more about it?

My advocacy is to Think Global and Act Local, encouraging people to decrease their carbon footprint as they go throughout their day. Even the most simple steps can make a significant contribution such as using reusable grocery bags and reducing household waste.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Chocolate every day, eek!
Q. We’re sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you consider your life goal?

I want to be able to make my mark in the film industry. I hope to fulfil this by taking every opportunity I can, not being afraid to fail, keeping my family and friends close and giving back as much as I can.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
1. A cure for every disease. 2. World acceptance of human differences. 3. To be with all my family overseas for a big happy reunion!
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

Always find a way to give back and protect the community so our future generations can enjoy the world we have around us today. For example, let’s take simple steps now and break the cycle of New Zealanders using 40,000 lightweight plastic bags every hour.

First, that women have equal rights like men everywhere in the world, second, health for everyone who are in great pain, and third, world without wars.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?
Stay good, enjoy and cheer for me on 21st of April 2018. ;)

title: Beauty talks with Miss Universe Croatia 2018 finalist Danijela Galekovic
dek: Miss Universe Croatia 2018 will organize its grand finale on 21st April 2018 where one out of the twenty finalists will be crowned as the successor of Miss Universe Croatia 2017 Shanaelle Petty.
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty talks with Miss Universe Croatia 2018 finalist Danijela Galekovic
paragraphs: Miss Universe Croatia 2018 will organize its grand finale on 21st April 2018 where one out of the twenty finalists will be crowned as the successor of Miss Universe Croatia 2017 Shanaelle Petty.
Before the finale, the contestant Danijela Galekovic finds time to share her experience and thoughts on her journey to Miss Universe Croatia 2018.
Below is her full Interview –
Q. How does it feel to be a delegate of Miss Universe Croatia 2018?

- Being a Miss Universe Croatia is really one of my dreams, and I feel honored to be given an opportunity to represent myself in the pageant. I will give my best during the preparations for the pageant and during the pageant. If I was to become a Miss Universe Croatia 2018 I would have been given an amazing platform to show the world what an amazing country Croatia is. It would also give me a platform to fulfill all of my dreams and the dreams of many other people who are desperately waiting for someone to help them in their hard life situations. All of these reasons above make me feel extremely blessed, proud and happy to be a delegate of Miss Universe Croatia 2018.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss Universe Croatia 2018?

- So far, I have learnt that whatever it is in life that you want to accomplish, you must always work hard for it. You must also always remain humble and no matter how big your success is, you must always be kind to people. Have an open mind and be willing to really hear what people are saying, but never forget who you are, and don’t let anyone change the essence of your being.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

- I think that every person has a gift for something, whether it is sport, arts, studying, etc. I always encourage people around me to not be scared of their dreams, and not to resist in pursuing them. Once you accomplish one of your goals, the feeling you get is non describing, it is beyond amazing. That exact feeling is what keeps me going every day, and pushes me even on the days when I feel like giving up. The journey towards the best version of yourself is the best journey you can be on in your lifetime.
Q. We would love to know more about your advocacy and what drove you to choose it?

- I would love to raise awareness of HIV, violence and obesity. I choose HIV awareness, because even though it is not the number 1 problem in my country, it is a big global problem, and I think that every girl that competes in her country’s Miss Universe pageant should think globally. HIV can be prevented so easily, but still there are so many who suffer from it, and I think the education is the key element here. The more people we teach how to stop HIV from spreading, the less ill people we will have, I believe. Next, I choose violence, because so many people suffer from violence, at schools, at home, at work. I want to let people know that they are not alone, that they are not in any way guilty for the violence they suffer from, and that the only way to run from it is to speak up. Everyone is worthy of love and dignity! Last, but not least, is obesity. Obesity is a raising problem in our society, with so many delicious and unhealthy foods available to us at almost every corner. I think that all habits are made at an early age, and that is why we need to educate parents on how to implement healthy habits into theirs and theirs children's lives. In that way, those children will grow up with healthy mindset about food and exercise, because they have learnt it from an early age. Also, we need to educate and help already obese children and grown ups on how to slowly but surely change their unhealthy habits into more healthy habits.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss Universe Croatia 2018?

- I will do my best to represent myself in the best possible way, and I hope that the judges and everyone else will capture who I truly am, and that is confident, kind, humble and hard working person. The best plan I have for the performance at the national stage at Miss Universe Croatia 2018 is to be myself. I have been preparing for this pageant ever since I went to a casting, I have been working out every single day and eating healthy even before I knew have I passed the casting or not.
Q. Who is your ideal, and what values of theirs do you wish you could inculcate in your own life, and teach the next generation?

- My idols are definitely my parents. They are both so hard working and full of love and patience. I try every day to inculcate their values into my life. From them I have inherited the love for animals and nature, admiration for small things, humbleness, kindness, willingness to always help others and hard working ethic. I would love to teach all the generations these values, because the more people we teach these values, the prettier the world will be.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

- If I could be invisible for a day, I would spend it around people who bully and therorize other people, because in that way I would probably realize what drives them to act in that way. By understanding that, maybe I could talk to them afterwards and resolve their inner problems, and they would finally start dealing with themselves instead of taking it out on other people. I believe that no one is born evil or with hatred, but people become that way because of their surroundings or perhaps some terrible events that occured to them during the lifetime.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

- There are 2 most special childhood memories of mine which I remember. First one is standing on my balcony with my parents and grandparents and watching those big colorful gas balloons taking off from the fields next from our house. They usually took off right before the sunset, and it was just magical. This event took place once a year, and I was always looking forward to it. The second memory is driving with my dad to a town near our hometown, on a beautiful spring day, passing by all the beautiful fields filled with sunflowers and flourished trees, and stopping by for our favourite ice creams on the way.
Q. What or who empowers you to be yourself and work hard every day?

- Well, my parents empower me to be myself and work hard everyday. They thought me from an early age how important it is to have a good working ethic and to accomplish something in your life, because no one can ever take your knowledge away from you. What also keeps me going is an idea of where I want to be in a couple of years, and I know that I have to work hard now to enjoy my results later. Also, I always remember to be myself, because that is what makes me special, otherwise we would all just be clones of one another and the world would be so boring.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

- Without a doubt, my biggest guilty pleasures are all kinds of delicious foods like cakes, hamburgers, fries, pizzas, chocolates, etc. I can say that I am a big food lover. I definitely have a very good self control to not to overindulge in these, because I want to obtain my health and a healthy weight, but every now and then I treat myself with these for all the hard work I put into.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

- My ultimate life goal is to become a successful business woman. My ideal life path would be to become a Miss Universe Croatia 2018 (and ultimately Miss Universe 2018) and a successful model, and one day start my own business and provide new working positions. With my profit , I would like to start new non-profit organizations or help existing ones, and in that way make a positive change in this world. If I would win Miss Universe Croatia 2018, I would have an amazing platform to bring this wishes to reality right away.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

- If I was granted 3 wishes right now, I would ask for all the wars and violence that is happening all around the world to stop, I would ask for all the hunger to stop because there is definitely too much food in the world today to still have people who are starving to death, and lastly, I would ask for all the illnesses to disappear.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

- I would like to take a moment to thank them for their support and interest for our lives. It really means a lot for us contestants to know that there are people who cheer for us, and it really gives us an extra boost of confidence and courage to persuade our dreams. Thank you all!

title: Beauty talks with Miss Belgium 2018 Angeline Flor Pua
dek: Miss Belgium 2018 Angeline Flor Pua was crowned on 13th January 2018 at Plopsa Theater de Panne, Belgium. Being the fifth Flemish in a row to win the title, Angeline bested 29 candidates to clinch the title of Miss Belgium 2018.
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty talks with Miss Belgium 2018 Angeline Flor Pua
paragraphs: Miss Belgium 2018 Angeline Flor Pua was crowned on 13th January 2018 at Plopsa Theater de Panne, Belgium. Being the fifth Flemish in a row to win the title, Angeline bested 29 candidates to clinch the title of Miss Belgium 2018.

At 22 years of age, she is in her third year of flying academy where she is studying to become a pilot. Even with her work commitments and her responsibilities as Miss Belgium 2018, she found time to share her thoughts, aspirations and experiences in the world of beauty pageants in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Below is her full interview –
Q. How does it feel to be crowned Miss Belgium 2018?
I feel so thankful and honoured to be crowned Miss Belgium 2018. It is like a dream come true and a reward of working hard for everyone that was involved.
Q.What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as a delegate in the Miss Belgium 2018 competition?

The best lesson I’ve learned is the hard work and to be yourself. My mother always told me ‘If you want to win, you have to work hard for it and that way you’ll earn it.’ For me, my perseverance was my asset in this competition.
Q.What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

My perseverance, I am a person that Is very goal oriented. If I want to accomplish something, I am the type of person that doesn’t give up easily until accomplished. Because Nelson Mandela once said, ‘A winner is a dreamer who never gives up’. I have a lot of people around me who are very supportive and it’s them where I put my focus on and get my inspiration. I am a strong woman and I am unstoppable.
Q.Recently, you faced some hateful racist comments after your crowning. How would you like to address that issue?

To be confronted with those comments hurts a lot. But I know those things they said are not true. I forgive them. I have a lot of people around me who are very supportive and it’s them where I put my focus on and get my inspiration.
Q.If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
I’ll just stay in the house haha and relax.
Q.Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?
The moment I knew that my mother was pregnant. I was incredibly happy that I was going to be a big sister. Someone I could take care of.
Q.How have your Filipino roots been a part of your journey till now?
My Filipino roots have been a big part of my journey. I have a lot of Filipino supporters/fans in Belgium who supported me and are still supporting my journey till now.
Q.You have achieved so much at such a young age. Can you tell us who you look up to in life?
I look up to my parents and Nelson Mandela. My parents have taught me a lot, that I should work hard to reach my dreams and to have faith in it, and to stay humble and to respect everyone.
I also look up to Nelson Mandela because he is a fighter. He fights for the people he cares no matter what. He is a good example for everyone.
Q.What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
My guilty pleasure; to eat French fries almost every day.
Q.We are sure that this competition is just another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

An international crown. I want to represent not only Belgium but the world without borders and to promote understanding and cooperation, and value education to achieve one's dream. I want to be a youth model. Through hard work, I want to be a pilot with a crown and travel around the world promoting my advocacy even after the pageant.
Q.If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
- Education access to everyone
- To help those in need
- Lastly, to fix all the broken pieces that humankind has created
Q.Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?
Thank you very much, for having this interview with me. For supporting me and I hope you keep supporting me through my journey. And I love your name Angelopedia <3

title: Beauty talks with Miss Montana USA 2018 Dani Walker
dek: Dani Walker was crowned Miss Montana USA 2018 at an event held at Missoula Children’s Theatre in Missoula, Montana last year. She is all set to represent Montana at the upcoming Miss USA 2018. As she trains for the finale, she finds time to share her…
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty talks with Miss Montana USA 2018 Dani Walker
paragraphs: Dani Walker was crowned Miss Montana USA 2018 at an event held at Missoula Children’s Theatre in Missoula, Montana last year. She is all set to represent Montana at the upcoming Miss USA 2018. As she trains for the finale, she finds time to share her thoughts, aspirations and experiences in the world of beauty pageants in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Q. How does it feel to be crowned as Miss Montana USA 2018?

Initially, it’s shocking. I woke up the next day, and several days after crowning, with the thought, “Did this really happen to me? I’m Miss Montana USA!?” It took several months to sink in, and now I feel an overwhelming sense of gratitude. As a titleholder, you get to experience, first hand, what it takes to prepare a titleholder for Miss USA. We work with numerous sponsors and receive an outpouring of support. Seeing behind the scenes gives me immense appreciation for all the sponsors and individuals, that make this journey possible for myself and other titleholders.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss USA 2018 in the competition?

I live by the quote, “Comparison is the thief of happiness.” Being a USA titleholder put that to the test. One of the most difficult aspects of the competition is a constant comparison by outside opinions. Fan pages online are wonderful, when they are rooting for you, but when they are not, it can affect your confidence. This year has been a test of my confidence, and it encouraged me to forge ahead with my life goals, and not concern myself with others expectations of my performance because I understand that winning or losing the title of Miss USA, is not directly tied to my potential for success in life.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

I am very fortunate because I had the unique experience of sharing my #roadtomissusa with people around the world, on my youtube channel youtube.com/daniwalker. The result of this was a multitude of support from viewers around the world that message me daily words of encouragement. They inspire me each day to live my best life, because this experience is now become our shared journey, and I want to do my best so I have the opportunity to share more with them.
Q. Is it true that you have been an advocate for the reduction of poverty since 2004? Would you like to tell us more about your initiative?

Yes, I grew up in a low-income household, and high-crime neighbourhood, with parents who were struggling to stay above the poverty line. When I was in jr. high, I began to grasp how difficult it is for individuals and families, like mine, to sustain a decent living, and that the issue of homelessness was more complex than finding employment. So I began volunteering my time, fundraising, and learning about this issue. To date, I have worked with over fifty non-profit organizations, most of which address issues related to poverty. From 2010-2015, I volunteered as a youth mentor in the Watts housing projects, which further peaked my interest in sustainable solutions for poverty. In my life, I devoted countless hours to this cause but wanted to find a way to use my reach as Miss Montana USA to get others involved, or at the very least, make them aware of this issue. I created the post for a purpose initiative, where I spotlight a new non-profit each day on Miss Montana USA social media. Since people are searching for my posts as a titleholder anyways, I wanted to expose them to something important and encourage them to share their #timetalenttreasure with an organization that touches their heart because we can make great strides to combat poverty when we work together.
Q. How would you like to represent yourself at the national stage at Miss USA 2018?

Authentically. I want people to see my personality on stage, and feel sincerity when I speak. The title of Miss USA took on new meaning after I decided to share my journey on Youtube. I am not merely representing myself on stage; I am standing in place of all the individuals like myself who are living in impoverished conditions or communities. If I can win the title of Miss USA, it will send a message to everyone who is facing similar circumstances that the opportunity gap in the United States is narrowing.
Q. We have got to know that music is a huge part of your life. What does music mean to you? Who is your favourite artist?

Music is self-expression to me. It enhances every moment of life. I’ve been performing publicly since high school, and I love to share my gifts with others because it brings us shared happiness. As for artists, I could listen to Amy Winehouse on repeat all day. Her voice is timeless to me.
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?

I would shadow other Youtubers for a day and learn more about the inner workings of their channels. I am always trying to bring better content to my subscribers, and there are endless amounts of skills to learn when it comes to creating remarkable content. I feel like I could learn a great deal from people who have larger channels than mine.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

One of my fondest memories growing up was spending time with my Nana and Tata, my mother’s parents. They too lived meagerly, but their home always felt warm. There was a palpable sense of love, and it taught me that happiness is not tied to tangible possessions.
Q. You’ve achieved so much not just as a pageant beauty but also as an enlightened citizen of the world. Can you tell us who you look up to in life?

I admire other self-made entrepreneurs, people who ignore naysayers and fearlessly pursue their passions. Elon Musk, of Tesla, is one such figure. He overcame seemingly insurmountable odds to bring Tesla cars to the market, and launch SpaceX rockets. People consistently tell him his vision is improbable, and he constantly proves them wrong. When I think of a difficult goal I want to accomplish, I ask myself, “is it harder than launching a rocket into space?” and when the answer is undoubtedly “no”, I feel confident that I can bring my own vision into reality.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?

I hate to admit it, but I do watch the Bachelor and the Bachelorette. I record the seasons and catch up on the episodes when I have a little downtime. I know it’s scripted but I think the show is hilarious with some heartwarming moments.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

I believe in dreaming big dreams, competing for Miss USA is the beginning of fantastic things to come. I want my name to be a global brand, with more products and services, designed to help others achieve their goals. My positivity-centred channel is devoted to sharing my knowledge, and my new online store helps women to dress for the job they want. My next goal is to release a phone app.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?

To be Miss Universe of course, but I think that one is a given. 2.) I would ask for women to be genuinely supportive of one another. Many ladies are missing out on incredible collaborations because they act out of scarcity. I catch myself regularly wishing this would change. 3.) Lastly, I wish for my Youtube channel to reach more people because I feel that it is a source of positive impact for those who watch it.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans of Angelopedia?

I would like to express my love and gratitude to all reading this. Thank you for caring enough to learn more about me. My hope is that my story can inspire you to do more, and be more because you too deserve to live your best life!
To know more about Dani Walker, follow her on her official Facebook page, Instagram, Youtube Channel, Twitter and website.

title: Beauty Talks with Kelley Johnson Miss California USA 2018
dek: (Photo Credits - Shana Lemos)
author: Priya Bhardwaj
caption: Beauty Talks with Kelley Johnson Miss California USA 2018
paragraphs: (Photo Credits - Shana Lemos)

Kelley Johnson is all set to represent California at the upcoming Miss USA 2018. As Kelley is training strenuously for the finale, she finds time to share her thoughts, aspirations and experiences in the world of beauty pageants in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Below is her full Interview -
Q. How does it feel to be crowned as Miss California USA 2018?

I feel prepared, humbled, and honoured. I worked very hard during the months before the pageant to prepare for the competition, and I have worked my entire life to become a woman that I believe was made for the job of Miss California USA. I was honoured and humbled that the judges saw that in me as well, and I am so excited for the year ahead.
Q. What is the best lesson you’ve learnt in your journey as the delegate of Miss USA 2018 in the competition?

The best lesson that I have learned in my journey to becoming Miss USA 2018 is that I cannot, should not, and will not compare myself to other contestants. I do not compete in pageantry against other women; I simply strive to show the world my best self and present the very best version of myself knowing that win or lose, I am enough to do the job of the titleholder. I hope that the judges on that day feel the same way.
Q. What is the one thing that keeps you going and inspires you to be the best version of yourself?

Self-motivation. I push to be the best version of myself for myself. I have to love who I am before anyone else can love who I am. However, it always feels good to make someone else’s day, and it is important to me to live every day with kindness for others.
Q. We have come to know that you really enjoy cooking and baking. What is the one thing that you could cook and eat forever?
I could cook cream cheese green chilli enchiladas forever, and I could eat ice cream every day for the rest of my life and be happy!
Q. If you could be invisible for a day, how would you like to spend it?
I would spend the day petting animals that would otherwise be dangerous, finding out the secret recipes at all my favourite restaurants, and sitting in the audience of all my favourite talk shows.
Q. Would you like to share your most special childhood memory with us?

My step-father would always take me on “adventures”. He never told me where we were going and would surprise me with really fun dinners and events. It was always just us, and he would even take me on school nights!
(Photo Credits - Kelley Johnson Instagram Official)
Q. You’ve achieved so much at such a young age. Can you tell us who you look up to in life?

I look up to strong, intelligent, kind, tolerant, and ambitious women. There are many, but to name a few: my mother, my sisters, Ellen DeGeneres, Michelle Obama, Jennifer Lawrence, Reese Witherspoon, Condoleezza Rice, Amal Clooney, etc.

Q. You are definitely one of the most experienced and accomplished pageant competitors this year at Miss USA 2018. Do you think experience gives an edge over other delegates in esteemed pageants such as Miss USA?

First of all, thank you! However, I do not think it gives me an edge over anyone else. I do think it gives me an edge over myself. National pageants come with a huge amount of pressure, stress, and competition. Having done this before, I feel incredibly level-headed, prepared, and confident going in. I know what to expect, I know what to do differently from before, and I believe in myself more than ever before. It gives you a sense of peace knowing that win or lose, you are content with who you are and what you bring to the organization.
Q. What is the one thing you can label as your guilty pleasure?
Restaurants. I love food, and I love eating out and trying new restaurants even if I just went grocery shopping.
Q. We’re sure that this competition is another milestone in your life. What is that one thing that you ultimately want to achieve?

I want to leave Miss USA knowing that the Miss Universe Organization and the judges knew everything I want them to know about me before making their decision about the next Miss USA. I feel very prepared and qualified to be Miss USA. I do not want to have any regrets, and that will come from showing them exactly who I am and what they would be getting if I was their next Miss USA. This way, if they do not choose me, I will be okay knowing there was nothing I could have done differently, and I will happily support our new titleholder.
Q. If you are granted 3 wishes right now, what would you ask for?
I would ask for good health, financial stability, and safety for all of my family, pets, and friends.
Q. Lastly, is there any message that you would like to give to your fans at Angelopedia?

I am thankful for your support, love, and kindness throughout my pageant career. I hope that I am always known as a contestant who put kindness before anything else, led with intelligence and strength, and never wavered in who she was authentically while competing despite what other people said. Go be the best YOU, that is who is going to win. There is nobody in the world that can tell you how to be you, and nobody has an exact recipe for winning pageants. People are drawn to women who know who they are, stand up for themselves, and are confident in what they bring to every table--even if what they bring is different than everyone else. Listen to your instincts and follow your heart. We are not defined by what other people think of us, we are defined by what we know to be true about ourselves.
All my love,
Kelley Johnson
You may also follow Kelley Johnson on her official Facebook page and Instagram account to know more about her and support her in her journey to Miss USA 2018.

title: Beauty Talks with Bojana Bojanić Miss Supranational Serbia 2017
dek: Bojana Bojanic is all set to represent Serbia in Miss Supranational 2017. As she is preparing herself for the big event, she finds time to share her thoughts, experiences and aspirations in the world of beauty pageants in an exclusive interview with…
author: Angelopedia
caption: Beauty Talks with Bojana Bojanić Miss Supranational Serbia 2017
paragraphs: Bojana Bojanic is all set to represent Serbia in Miss Supranational 2017. As she is preparing herself for the big event, she finds time to share her thoughts, experiences and aspirations in the world of beauty pageants in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia.
Below is her full interview -
Q. How does it feel to represent Serbia in Miss Supranational 2017?

It’s such an honour to represent the beauty of my country at a prestigious pageant like Miss Supranational. I am happy that a contest is in Europe, so my family and friends will be able to come and cheer for me.
Q. How are you preparing for Miss Supranational 2017?

Miss Supranational is one of the biggest events in my life. I am a perfectionist and I want to prepare myself to the maximum. Recently, I participated in a fashion show showcasing works of the most famous Serbian designers, and soon I will travel to India where I will promote my title and Serbia. I am trying to stay true to myself, yet always open to learn and improve. I work hard and I never give up on my dreams.
Q. Would you like to share your feelings on not participating in Miss Universe 2017?

I have to admit that I am very sorry that I will not participate in Miss Universe. But on the other hand, I am very thankful to have the opportunity to go to Miss Supranational! They say “when one door closes, a new and much better one opens“.
Q. What inspired you to become a model and enter beauty pageants?

I have been in the world of fashion since I was eight years old. And I was always interested in the beauty contests, so at the recommendation of my mother, I decided to apply for Miss Serbia. For me, Miss Supranational is a great promotion for young girls, their cultures and ideas how to positively influence the changes in the world.
Q. What is the most important lesson you have learned from your modelling career?

I learned that being confident is the key to life. Don't be afraid to be you! I am super different from a lot of girls in style and personality, and I am OK with it. And if you are OK with it, everyone else will be too. Just be and love yourself!
Q. What do you aspire to become in life?

My biggest wish is to become a police officer, to stop criminals and murders. My late father was a soldier, my mom is a member of police; and since I was three, I knew what I want to be when I grow up! And of course, there is a big wish to become Miss Supranational 2017 and to show the beauty of my country!
Q. You have been actively involved in humanitarian causes. What inspires you to do so?

I accidentally started charity work by watching TV shows where they were saying that children need financial help. Then I looked at my little brother and wondered what would I do if he needed that kind of help. I realized that I must help as much as I can. Then I organized a charity fashion show. When the money was collected, I received a call from the mother of little Sara. Her family made a decision for her to first hear my voice after surgery. It was the most emotional moment in my life.
Q. How do you react to media associating you with different people in a romantic relationship?
I really don’t like to talk about my private life in public. Medias exist to write and sell papers and they just have to write about someone. I don’t pay any attention to it.
Q. What is that one thing you love the most in life?
I love my family the most! They are my biggest support, my reliance and my motivation. They will forever be my number one. I admire my mom and dad and I would love to accomplish their expectations!
Q. If you win the title of Miss Supranational 2017, what is the first thing you would like to do or change?
It would be a great honour to win the title. I would like to talk more about the problems of woman abuse and the difficulties of the treatment of children with rare diseases.
Q. What suggestions would you like to give to aspiring beauty queens?
My mom once said to me, 'Work hard and be patient.' It was the best advice she ever gave me. You have to put the hours in. And also, be happy for this moment. This moment is your life.
Q. What message would you like to give to your fans on Angelopedia?

I would like to thank them for a big support and motivation they are giving me. That amount of love that I am receiving from them makes me give all of myself and to show them they were right in trusting me!

title: Beauty Talks with Sophia Koch Miss Universe Germany 2017
dek: Sophia Koch, the 20-year-old gorgeous model from Germany, was crowned Miss Universe Germany 2017 at the finale of the pageant held on 24th September 2017. Sophia, besides being a professional model, is a student of sociology and German literature at the…
author: Angelopedia
caption: Beauty Talks with Sophia Koch Miss Universe Germany 2017
paragraphs: Sophia Koch, the 20-year-old gorgeous model from Germany, was crowned Miss Universe Germany 2017 at the finale of the pageant held on 24th September 2017. Sophia, besides being a professional model, is a student of sociology and German literature at the Martin Luther University.

With almost perfect facial features and an hourglass figure, she will surely make a positive impression at Miss Universe 2017 competition. In an exclusive interview with Angelopedia, Sophia unveils her personality and shares her experiences and aspirations in the world of modelling and beauty pageants. Behind an astonishingly beautiful face and modelesque features, lies a beautiful heart of a simple girl, who is family-oriented and enjoys simple things in life.
Below is her full interview -
Q. How does it feel after winning the Miss Universe Germany 2017 title?

It is such big honour for me and what makes me feel most happy and motivated is the support and faith in me that comes from all over the world. It still feels unreal to me because it is this big opportunity and I think I am starting to realize everything more and more when I will be in Las Vegas.
Q. Would you like to share anything about your preparations for Miss Universe 2017?

I am really focused on myself to be the best version of myself and I practice regularly, especially my catwalk. I am watching my diet and I am having a fitness routine with my personal coach as well. I also watch a lot of Miss Universe shows from the last years to get even more excited and prepare better for the pageant next month.
Q. What is your interpretation of the Miss Universe logo - "the woman with stars“?

One of my interpretations is that the women, who get to win the Miss Universe title at a country level or at the international platform, can reach for the stars, dream big and make their dreams come true. No matter what she is aspiring, she just has to go for it. My second interpretation is that as an aspiring beauty queen, a girl aiming for the Miss Universe crown is giving everything that is in her power to reach these stars and make her dream come true.
Q. Who do you look up to in life for inspiration?

I am always looking up to my parents because they are in every way my role models. My mother is so optimistic, positive and strong as well as my father. I received so much love and happiness in my childhood until this day and I see what kind of person I became because of it. I want to be like them if I have the luck to be a mother one day and make my children feel proud of me like I feel proud of my parents.
Q. Who is your favourite Miss Universe and why?

I believe that every single Miss Universe has been amazing in her own individual way. But Pia Wurtzbach has a really beautiful look, appearance and heart, and that makes her to my favourite Miss Universe.
Q. From where do you derive your confidence?

I got my confidence from the people that surrounded me throughout my life and these are especially my parents, family and friends. They always made me feel appreciated, loved and gave me the feeling that I am able to achieve my goals and dreams because I am beautiful the way I am. They believed in me and that made me believe in myself in a confident way as well.
Q. Can you share the most memorable moment of your life?

The most memorable moment in my life is a dinner I had with my father a few years ago in Porto, Portugal, when we were staying there for vacation. These are kind of moments where everything comes together so perfectly that you cherish to relive even years! We were sitting in this restaurant directly at the beach behind a huge glass wall all alone, no other guests were there. The sun went down, so while we were eating we got to see the most beautiful sunset you could dream of. We were so happy and thankful for this moment and the life we get to live.
Q. Can you share something that you are passionate about?

I am really passionate about making others happy. I am always putting a lot of work and dedication to it because when I see a face that is happy because of me it makes my whole day better. Because of that I really like to help wherever and whenever I can and as well I do everything that it takes to make my loved ones around me feel really special and loved.
Q. What is that one thing that keeps you going?

The one thing that keeps me going is the support of the people that always stood behind me and believed in me since day one. They are the people I want to make proud and show them that it hasn't been a waste of time having faith in me.
Q. If you win the title of Miss Universe 2017, what is the first thing you would like to do or change?

I want to work for the betterment and uplifting of children, who are underprivileged or abused or with special needs or have any other problem in their lives. I would like to create a platform for such children all over the world and create a huge system of support for them no matter what they have gone through.

This is a massive task, but I want to start somewhere to change a lot of things for them to make their lives better. Children are our next generation that will hold the world in their hands and have the power to move it in the right direction and to give the children the right direction, education is the key. Education starts by providing components for children that live in poverty and have limited resources. These components can help to find children’s interests, their passions and develop their dreams more and more.

I want to help children that have been mistreated and feel worthless. I want to support them in a way that they see life again with a different point of few and make them believe in their self again. I want to make them clear that it will always be up to them where they can reach or what they can achieve in their lives and make them feel motivated again no matter how they have been treated in the past.

I also want to include professional psychologists in this project and platform that can help children especially when they have been abused. I believe that we have to guide our next generation from now on, give them the opportunity to develop their own individual personality with interests and dreams and especially provide help if they are on a wrong path.
Q. What inspired you to become a model and enter beauty pageants?

I always had a passion for posing and presenting myself in front of a camera. I think that it is just in my nature. The world of beauty pageants is really new to me, but I fell in love the whole idea behind it that you can do so much more with your beauty. I really have the intention to use the title in the best way possible to make a lot of things in our world change for the better.
Q. Can you say 3 words that describe your journey so far?
Exciting, Rollercoaster, Enchanting!
Q. Why do you think Germany has not won any Miss Universe title after Marlene Schmidt's victory in 1961?

I feel that beauty pageants are not a big cultural thing in Germany like in other big nations of our world. I also believe that there is a lack of knowledge when it comes to pageants here in Germany and because of that, it is harder to find people that really support a girl who goes to international beauty pageants. A win this time may change the way people look at beauty pageants in Germany!
Q. What suggestions would you like to give to aspiring beauty queens?

Be yourself and believe in the beauty of your genuineness. I want you to do things for you, that make you feel better and not because other people want and expect certain things from you. Beauty has so many different faces and it may start with the outside of a person but goes so much deeper when you really want to see how beautiful someone is by looking into their hearts, souls and personalities. Be the best version of yourself and feel confident with it because if you love yourself, everyone else will do the same.
Q. What message would you like to give to your fans on Angelopedia?

It is still overwhelming to see all of your positive feedback and the love you have sent me from all over the world. You can't believe how much your comments and messages make my day and I want to let you know that I appreciate every single one of them. If you need something you can always come to me and write me, I try to answer all the time. I hope you are happy and feel loved.
Sending you kisses from Germany and I will make you proud!

title: Beauty Talks with Elisabeta Eliza Ancău Miss Global Charity Queen 2017
dek: The stunning Romanian beauty, Elisabeta Eliza Ancau was crowned Miss Global Charity Queen 2017 recently. The lovely queen, who works as a model at EuroModels agency, Romania is a graduate of the Babes-Bolyai University (Faculty of Political, Administrative…
author: Angelopedia
caption: Beauty Talks with Elisabeta Eliza Ancău Miss Global Charity Queen 2017
paragraphs: The stunning Romanian beauty, Elisabeta Eliza Ancau was crowned Miss Global Charity Queen 2017 recently. The lovely queen, who works as a model at EuroModels agency, Romania is a graduate of the Babes-Bolyai University (Faculty of Political, Administrative and Communication Sciences) in Cluj-Napoca, Romania. This beauty deeply feels for the people with special needs, as she was born in in a family with deaf parents and she has been involved in social work and charity since a young age.

Miss Global Charity Queen 2017 is not her first attempt in the world of beauty pageants. Last year, she represented Romania in Miss Global Beauty Queen 2017 held in South Korea. She was a whisker away from winning the crown which was won by Vietnamese beauty Nguyen Thi Ngoc Duyen, and Eliza finished at the second place. Prior to that, she was also crowned Miss Supranational Romania 2015 and represented Romania in Miss Supranational 2015.

The beautiful Eliza shared her thoughts, experiences, and aspirations in the world of pageantry with Angelopedia in an interview. We would like to thank her for sparing time to talk to us and provide an insight into her veiled personality.
Below is her full interview -
Q. Congratulations on being crowned as Miss Global Charity Queen 2017. How does it feel after winning the title?
Thank you very much! My heart is filled with joy and gratitude. I ticked another step, other responsibilities and a new achievement. I can only be glad.
Q. The world celebrates you as Miss Global Charity Queen, but would you like to give us a glimpse of your veiled personality?
I am a simple person, modest, sensitive, independent and ambitious. I think I have a strong personality, so I get almost everything I want. I like to trust people, so I might be slightly naive.
Q. Would you like to share your experience in the beautiful Penghu, where Miss Global Charity Queen 2017 took place?

An unforgettable experience! The heat outside was blistering but everything else was extremely pleasant. Penghu is a beautiful island with delicious seafood and warm people. They have a very good Mayor that is dedicated to the locals and who gets involved in the development of the region.
Q. How do you plan to fulfil your responsibility as ambassador for 2018 Most Beautiful Bays World Congress?

This beauty contest has given me the opportunity to be present in a wonderful place like the Penghu Islands. My responsibility this year is to convey my experiences and my accumulated knowledge about this location. The technology of today is so advanced that we are able to provide a wide audience with accurate information and visual news about places, food, people and tourism.
Q. What are your career plans after winning the pageant?
After this win, I am following the same ideals of becoming a successful businesswoman. Last year we started a small family business and now we are expanding it and I hope it grows well.
Q. What was your motivation behind stepping into the world of beauty pageants?

Honestly, there was no a specific motivation. I entered this world in 2015, pushed by my manager. Only then I discovered that I have qualities for this and now I can say that this world does fascinate me.
Q. What do you think is the most important thing to win a beauty pageant?
To win, I think femininity, self-confidence, attitude, punctuality, seriousness and involvement are very important.
Q. What are you most passionate about in life?
Passions come in turn. Once I was passionate about playing basketball, now I am passionate about the beautiful, and for me the beautiful means art, the journey, the people and the divinity.
Q. Would you like to share some uniquely saccharine moments of your childhood with us?
My childhood was quite different. What I can tell you is that I was born in a family with hearing deficiencies, my parents are deaf and my past is full of beautiful though difficult experiences.
Q. What is your greatest strength in life?
To understand, listen and help as much as I can those in need. The important thing is to remain positive whatever happens, and life will give you a lot of energy.
Q. What according to you is the most amazing thing about Romania?
I can say a lot about my country. In brief, I can say that we have a delicious kitchen, beautiful landscapes, clean air, welcoming people and the mysterious air of Dracula’s lands.
Q. If you had to describe your “perfect man”, what traits of his personality would be written in bold?

The man who knows how to be a man, who can offer respect, devotion and understanding. If the man does not have fluctuations in character and can support me intellectually, I get to be more productive and loving.
Q. If not a beauty queen, what would you have aspired to be?

For me to be a beauty queen is a gift, not an aspiration. Every person has a title in life, even my mother who is simply a mother has a difficult title because today it is harder to keep a family together. In the future, I aspire to be a positive example for women.
Q. If there were no rules in your life for a day, what all would you do?

Believe me, there are days when I live by my own rules. There are those moments when I want to detach myself from what causes me negative states, those days when I play as the heart says. Sometimes, too much reasoning drains us.
Q. What suggestions would you like to give to aspiring beauty queens?

My suggestions are to be as normal as possible, to trust themselves and their own strengths, to smile as much as possible, to be positive in any situation, and to not copy the style of other women. Be yourself and nothing more!
Q. What message would you like to give to your fans on Angelopedia?

I thank Angelopedia fans for watching this platform, which wants to provide the audience not only with pictures of beautiful girls in beauty contests but also with facts about their lives. The interviews are written in detail in order to provide the public with more information about the contestants than any other Miss-related page.
We, on behalf of all the fans of Angelopedia, wish you good luck in achieving your dreams in life and hope that you will continue with your efforts to help the people with special needs.
Thank You, Eliza!

title: Beauty Talks with Andjelija Rogić Miss World Serbia 2017
dek: Andjelija Rogic (Andelija Rogic), who was crowned Miss Srbije 2016 (Miss Serbia 2016/ Miss World Serbia 2017) is all set to compete in Miss World 2017 as the representative of Serbia. She is 23 years old and stands tall at an impressive height of 175 cm.
author: Angelopedia
caption: Beauty Talks with Andjelija Rogić Miss World Serbia 2017
paragraphs: Andjelija Rogic (Andelija Rogic), who was crowned Miss Srbije 2016 (Miss Serbia 2016/ Miss World Serbia 2017) is all set to compete in Miss World 2017 as the representative of Serbia. She is 23 years old and stands tall at an impressive height of 175 cm.

Andjelija finished her studies in nursing and is currently a student of Pedagogy, which looks at educating children and has ambitions to be successful in her chosen field. Her hobbies are playing volleyball, music, dancing, cooking and acting. Ever since she was crowned Miss Serbia 2016, she has been involved in humanitarian work and promoting education. Her personal motto is 'If you believe you can achieve!"

On her way to China to compete in Miss World 2017, she shared her thoughts, experiences and aspirations in the world of pageantry in an exclusive interview with Angelopedia. Thank you Andjelija for finding time for this interview, while you were already on your way to China, and we wish you all the best for Miss World 2017!
Below is her full interview.
Q. How does it feel to represent Serbia in the most prominent international pageant?

Being a Miss Serbia is a great honour and privilege for me, but is also a responsibility. It gave me the opportunity to be a role model for young girls and the ability to positively affect the problems in our society. I am very excited and I can not wait to meet all the contestants.
Q. Would you like to share anything about your preparations for Miss World 2017?

This year is certainly one of the most important in my life. The title of Miss Serbia enabled me to travel, meet new cultures and people. I am proud of the numerous humanitarian activities in which I participated. For the talent competition, I have prepared a very interesting performance that connects dance and painting. I made the national costume by myself and also gift for a humanitarian auction.
Q. What is your 'Beauty with a Purpose' project for Miss World 2017?

My 'Beauty with a Purpose' project is related to my profession. As a teacher, I would like the children to be provided with free education, to freely develop their talents and creativity. We live in the internet era, and it needs to be better used to connect teachers and children. Children are the world's most valuable resource and its best hope for the future.
Q. What inspired you to become a model and enter beauty pageants?

The interesting thing is that my best friend sent the application for the Miss Serbia contest. The rest is history, I won the title and got the opportunity to represent my country in China. I have been working as a model for several years and I worked for one of the most famous European and Serbian designers.
Q. Who do you look up to in life for inspiration?
I find inspiration in children. They are always honest, happy and smiling. In their eyes, the world is a magical place to play.
Q. Who is your favourite Miss World and why?

My favourite Miss World is Aishwarya Rai. Her accomplishments in the field of fashion, cinema, social work and promoting her country at an International level, has been tremendous. She is such a role model!
Q. From where do you derive your confidence?
Nothing can be done without hope and confidence. For me, optimism is the faith that leads to achievement.
Q. Can you share the most memorable moment of your life?
That would probably be the moment when I found out that I would get a younger brother. I was so happy!
Q. Can you share something that you are passionate about?
I’m very passionate about local folklore and handicrafts in my area. I hold the position of 'Guardian' of my local folk culture and heritage.
Q. What is that one thing that keeps you going?
I believe that love is the driving force of everything.
Q. If you win the title of Miss World 2017, what is the first thing you would like to do or change?
As I mentioned before, I would fight for the free education for all children in the world. I would also like to establish a creative centre for talented kids in Serbia.
Q. Can you say 3 words that describe your journey so far?
Experience, Patience and Maturity
Q. If you can choose which designer will design your gown for Miss World finale, who will it be and why?

Elie Saab is my favourite designer and it would be such an honour to wear his gown. He is able to combine his love of his homeland with love of the west into beautiful fashions that encompass the best of both worlds.
Q. Why do you think Serbia has not won any Miss World title so far?

Serbia is a country of beautiful women and it is truly disappointing that we did not make any major success on Miss World. I hope this will change in the future because we have great potential. Maja Smiljkovic is very much noticed at Miss Grand International, Marija Nikic is one of the favourites at Miss Earth, and Bojana Bojanic will do great at Miss Supranational.
Q. What suggestions would you like to give to aspiring beauty queens?
Just be yourself, and enjoy the blessings that God has given you.
Q. What message would you like to give to your fans on Angelopedia?

I want to thank all readers who support every girl at beauty contests. Your support means a lot to us and pushes us to be even better. I hope you're cheering for me at Miss World, and I'll try to do my best!

title: Beauty Talks with Christina Lazaros, Finalist Miss Intercontinental Nederland 2017
dek: Christina Lazaros is competing this year in Miss Intercontinental Nederland. She is 21 years of age and is a student of law. Having lived in the Netherlands for almost all her life, except for 3 years in Greece when she was very young, she has become…
author: Angelopedia
caption: Beauty Talks with Christina Lazaros, Finalist Miss Intercontinental Nederland 2017
paragraphs: Christina Lazaros is competing this year in Miss Intercontinental Nederland. She is 21 years of age and is a student of law. Having lived in the Netherlands for almost all her life, except for 3 years in Greece when she was very young, she has become passionate about pageantry over the last few years. She started competing in beauty pageants in 2013. Before competing for Miss Intercontinental Nederland 2017, she also competed in Miss Grand Nederland 2017, Miss World Nederland 2016 and Miss Eco Universe 2016.
In an interview with Angelopedia, Christina shared her thoughts, aspirations and experiences in the world of pageantry. Below is the transcript of Angelopedia's interview with Christina Lazaros -
Q. How does it feel to compete in Miss Intercontinental Nederland 2017?

It feels magical! The past years I always watched the girls competing in Miss Beauty of The Netherlands from the sideline, wishing I would be on that stage one day. Now that I've won the Miss Intercontinental of Groningen title and that I am in the running to win the national title, I feel so excited! I enjoy every moment of my journey towards this title as I learn so much and I can't wait for the big day to come.
Q. You have participated in several beauty pageants before, does that make you more confident to win this title?

I think having done pageants before can be an advantage, but also a disadvantage. Doing pageants, in general, has given me a lot of self-confidence and because for example, I have walked the catwalk several times before, this makes me more confident. On the other hand, I feel like there's so much more to learn. I taught myself a lot about pageants by watching YouTube video's and reading articles, but never really had a coach or national director telling me exactly what to do. I am very grateful for the Miss Beauty of The Netherlands organisation for giving me a chance. I don't feel like they judge me on the hand of having done pageants before, but give me a fair chance like all other contestants.
Q. You were so close to winning the Miss World Nederland 2016 crown, how did you feel about not winning it finally?

To be honest, I was happily surprised by winning the place of 2nd runner up as I did not expect to win the title that day at all! I was very proud of myself and was determined to continue doing pageants. It was really nice to have some sort of confirmation to know that what I am doing is right.
Q. Who was your role model behind stepping into the world of beauty pageants?

When I was 16 years old I watched Lauraine van der Werff winning ''Miss Drenthe'' on TV. I watched her shining on stage which I adored because when I was a little child I used to perform in front of my family. I was always singing and dancing and loved to be the centre of attention. I think from the moment I watched Lauraine, I started to dive into the pageant world. When I was 17 years old I competed in my first pageant and won a wildcard to compete in the Miss Drenthe pageant, like Lauraine did.
Q. Would you like to give us a glimpse of your veiled personality?

As a person I easily make friends. Even if I only know you for a few days, I am sincerely interested in who you are and always want to help if you let me. I like to see through people and get to know different cultures and ways of thinking. Also, I am compassionate, spontaneous and I am always in for a laugh!
Q. Would you like to share some uniquely saccharine moments of your childhood with us?

Like I mentioned before, I used to perform in front of my family a lot! I and my sister always watched a TV-programme called ''The mini playback-show'' in which children were performing as their favourite singer. My grandmother recorded the show on video for us. We could watch the video over and over again. We never got tired of it! Being the centre of attention is something I loved from when I was a little girl. I always gave little performances to my family.
Q. Tell us something that most people don’t know about you?

If I didn't study Law School, I'd love to work for Disney! In my spare time (back in the days where I didn't have to study so much) I used to draw and I loved the thought of making a career in doing what I like to do.
Q. If you had to describe your “perfect man”, what traits of his personality would be written in bold?
I don't believe anyone is perfect, but to me, a man who is self-confident, spontaneous, reliable, and has humour would be close to perfect. Those four characteristics are really important to me.
Q. What according to you define femininity? Who is the most treasured female figure in your life?

To me, femininity is when you can walk around confident and can be proud of who you are. Femininity is when you trust yourself in the things you can accomplish as a woman, which I believe is a lot. Being a woman is a wonderful gift and I believe every woman on this planet has something beautiful, no matter what size, colour, age, race or whatsoever.

There is more than one female figure who I treasure in my life. Starting off with my mother who is a very strong woman, but I also love my grandmother and sister a lot. I can't imagine life without them.
Q. If you were invisible for a day, what all would you do?

If I were invisible for a day, I would go to a luna-park or water park and go in all roller-coasters and water slides without having to stand in this long queue or having to buy this expensive fast-pass, haha!
Q. If you could define yourself with a “colour”, what colour would you choose and why?

I would choose the colour light blue which is my favourite colour. Light blue and crystal clear as the sky is, I think I am an open book and when you have a place in my heart or life, you can fully trust me and see right through me.
Q. If you had to change one thing in your past, what would it be and why?

I think the past has made me who I am today and so, if I would change something, I wouldn't be who and where I am now. I am content with who I am and I believe I learned from my past, whether this was good or bad. I believe you should always look forward and don't stick too much to the past if this was a bad one. It's up to yourself if you better yourself as a person or not.
Q. What is special and unique about Dutch women?

Dutch women are very down-to-earth. We have a saying in The Netherlands that sounds - "Just act normal because when you do, you already act crazy enough.'' I think this soberness helps us to calm down in stressful situations. Because of this, I consider Dutch beauty queens like Trojan horses; they seem very calm during pageants, but behind this down-to-earth mind, there's a great plan on winning a title. We are not easily distracted and have our mind set, while we make fun and relax.
Q. What suggestions would you like to give to aspiring beauty queens?

To always believe in yourself, which mind sound cliché, but which is true! I started doing pageants all by myself and though I never won, I kept going on and on, because I was and am sure that my time would come. Now I've won my first actual crown, Miss Intercontinental Groningen, and I'm determined to go for the national title. My dream is to go to a big international pageant and I truly believe that I can.
Q. What message would you like to give to your fans on Angelopedia?

To always believe in yourself! I keep repeating it, but I truly believe that you can accomplish anything as long as you believe in yourself and work hard for what you want. Keep that goal in mind and you will see that you will be rewarded, whether this is what you actually wanted or the feeling of satisfaction when you know you have done everything in order to say "I can be proud of myself.'' Never give up on your dreams, I also don't.
